News.title: Dad finds son, 3, ‘in pool of blood’ after plunging 65ft from Cyprus apartment as post mortem reveals horror injuries
News.content:
FALL TRAGEDY Dad finds son, 3, ‘in pool of blood’ after plunging 65ft from Cyprus apartment as post mortem reveals horror injuries

A DISTRAUGHT dad has told how he found his three-year-old son in a “pool of blood” after he plunged 65ft from a Cyprus apartment.

The child’s post-mortem has revealed he suffered “severe cranial injuries” and body blows that would have killed him instantly after he fell to his death from a sixth-floor balcony.



Experts concluded the three-year-old’s vital organs were also shattered when he fell 65ft from his parents’ flat in Nicosia, the island’s capital.

The report by Angeliki Papeta and Orthodox Orthodoxou concluded: “Death was a result of the fall.”



In the coming days further tests will be conducted on blood samples and other organs, they said.

The horrific tragedy is thought to have unfolded when the child climbed through a window onto a closed balcony in the block of flats on Saturday evening.



Police arrested his parents on suspicion of causing death by negligence.

They told police they had left the window open because of the unusually hot temperatures Cyprus has endured in recent weeks.

The boy’s dad described how “panic stricken” he had rushed to pick up his son lying “in a pool of blood.”

Cypriot cops said Monday the parents had been detained “in the interests of clarity” as authorities conducted their inquiry.



The family also have a younger daughter.

Police spokesman Vyron Vyronas called the boy’s death “a tragic incident,” explaining that “every measure” had been taken to look after the younger child.

He said: “The parents have been detained for five days to assist our inquiry.

“It was considered necessary even though we understand their grief and emotional turmoil but all sides have to be examined.”

It comes after a Brit toddler fell to his death from a hotel window in Paphos on July 12.



Cypriot authorities were slammed for the way they treated the child’s Brit dad after his son fell out of a fourth-floor window.

The two-year-old boy died at a luxury hotel after allegedly slipping from his dad’s arms and falling 33ft to the veranda below.

The 37-year-old city executive has filed an official request for dismissal with the Attorney General of Cyprus as he faces accusations of causing the death of his son by a reckless act.

He was arrested at the resort and jailed for eight days. He was then charged, released on bail and allowed to return to the UK to attend his son’s funeral.

The Essex-born man, who works at a big four consultancy firm, will appear in court this Thursday to answer charges of “recklessly” causing his son’s death.



If convicted, he faces a prison sentence of up to four years.

Alexandros Alexandrou, the father’s lawyer, stressed there was no public interest in prosecuting the grieving father and that a prolonged prosecution would further traumatise the family.

He said: “We have asked the attorney-general to discontinue this prosecution on public interest and humanitarian grounds.

“In these exceptional circumstances we do not believe a continued criminal process serves the public interest.

“The family has already suffered an unimaginable loss, and the focus now should be on their welfare and recovery.”

News.title: Posh glamping site hit by complaints over noisy couples romping all night after late-night drinking WINS bid to expand
News.content:
BONK BATTLE Posh glamping site hit by complaints over noisy couples romping all night after late-night drinking WINS bid to expand

A POSH glamping site has won a battle to expand despite neighbours complaining about noisy couples romping all night.

Elizabeth Pengelly initially wanted to add more tents to her Welsh farm – Swallows Nest – before it was turned down over fears of noise from amorous couples and late-night drinking.



But now planners have instead given the green light to shepherd’s huts at the farm and moved them further away from homes.

Swallow’s Nest already has two shepherd huts in use for glamping along with a herd of alpacas – and originally wanted to add more tents in the countryside at Abergavenny, Monmouthshire.



But Labour councillor Dale Rooke said the tents would also be too close to the neighbouring property.

He told planners: “Tents are naturally not soundproofed so any shenanigans going on inside will be heard in the wider vicinity.”



But applicant Elizabeth Pengelly submitted a new plan to add one more shepherds hut and washroom on wheels so they can be stored in winter.

Ms Pengelly also insisted rules would be put in place to protect neighbours from noise from the site at Hardwick.



Monmouthshire Council has approved the new plans.

The council previously received a series of objections from neighbours – with some claiming sex noises were keeping them up at night.

Yvonne and Brian Saddler, who have lived next door to the field for 32 years spoke of their upset.

“We moved here those years ago because it is so peaceful and beautiful,” said Mr Saddler, 91.

“You never used to hear any noise other than the birds singing and it has been glorious, until now.



“Our garden backs onto the field and when people are staying in the shepherd huts, we can hear every word they’re saying – and not all of it is the kind of stuff we want to be listening to. There’s often a lot of swearing and drinking going on.”

Retired engineer Brian said: “If they had been granted permission for the camping site, our lives would’ve been an utter misery. I don’t want that sort of thing going on next door.”

His 90 year-old wife, Yvonne, a retired factory worker, agreed.



She said: “We’ve heard people’s fears about couples getting romantic late at night, but to be honest that wouldn’t affect us because we’re usually in bed by 8 o’clock.

“Our bigger concern was the volume of traffic the site would have generated.

“There’s only a narrow, single lane road running up here and if you’ve got a dozen or so extra vehicles using it night and day, it would have led to a lot of noise and frustrations.

“It just isn’t an appropriate place for a business of this kind.”

When The Sun visited the village last month, locals whose homes overlook Swallows Nest were quick to spell out their objections.



One resident told us: “We live right next door to this field and we hear everything.

“We hear them shouting and playing loud music, and then we have to put up with the sound of them getting amorous when they go to bed,” they added.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I am no killjoy, but I just don’t want to be living right next door to what sometimes sounds like an orgy.”

The Swallows Nest site is less than two miles away from Abergavenny, which has a 13,000 population and an array of shops, restaurants, bars and hotels.

News.title: Baby boy, 11 months, left in care of 19-year-old ‘babysitter’ found dead just hours after child reported missing
News.content:
AN 11-month-old baby has been found dead just hours after he was reported missing in a small town with a population under 200 people.

Grayson Walton was reportedly left in the care of a 19-year-old while his father was at work.



Family members of baby Grayson said on Saturday night the 11-month-old was last seen in Cleaton, Kentucky.

Cleaton is a small town in the southern part of the state located in Muhlenberg County, with a population of 168, according to the 2020 census.



The Central City Police Department said on Monday they responded to a “reported disturbance” at a home in the 800 block of Harrison Avenue in Cleaton.

Officials spoke with the baby’s father at the home on Saturday just after 5pm.

read more on news GRIM DISCOVERY Missing newlywed, 35, found dead days after vanishing without cellphone



The father said Grayson was supposed to be in the care of 19-year-old Elijah Mayes while he was at work, according to police.

Mayes told investigators that a family friend had picked up the infant around 10pm on Friday night.

“Officers located and interviewed that individual, who stated that she had not picked up the child,” the department said.

A relative told police they saw Mayes with the child on Friday in the 300 block of Hillview Street, roughly four miles away from where police spoke with Grayson’s father.



Investigators obtained a search warrant for the home where police first met with the father and allegedly found methamphetamine inside the residence.

A second search warrant was then executed for the residence where Mayes was allegedly last seen with Grayson, where they found the 11-month-old dead.

Mayes has since been arrested and charged with murder, first-degree criminal abuse, tampering with physical evidence, abuse of a corpse and possession of a methamphetamine.

The investigation remains ongoing.



“Additional information will be released when appropriate and as the investigation allows,” the local police department said.

One woman who identified herself as Grayson’s aunt on Facebook, said she believed Grayson went missing sometime in the middle of the night on Friday, and said she learned of his disappearance around 5pm on Saturday.

Just before 11am on Sunday, the aunt said Grayson had been found.

Loved ones had asked people on social media not to speculate about the matter.



The U.S. Sun has reached out to the family and local authorities for comment.

News.title: Britain must prepare for Russian drones to swarm skies – ‘attempted strike on Boris’ was just warning shot, experts fear
News.content:
BRITAIN must prepare for Russian drones to swarm our skies as Vladimir Putin turns his crosshairs to European nations supporting Ukraine, experts warn.

The alleged attempted strike on Boris Johnson’s train was just a warning shot as Moscow draws the UK into a direct “militarised confrontation” that could erupt at any moment.



Speaking to Sam Homewood in The Sun’s new studio in the heart of the newsroom, military analyst Michael Clarke told The Sun: “Russia is getting very, very close to committing real violence against the rest of us, not just the Ukrainians.

“What they’re trying to say is, ‘you’re playing with fire. We’re on the road to war’.”



The ex-PM was travelling close to the Polish border in Ukraine when the service behind his was blown up by Russian forces on Sunday.

Ukraine’s railway operator later revealed Johnson’s train had left ahead of schedule amid fears of Russian strikes.

Ukrzaliznytsia said in a post on Telegram it was “quite possible” that the drone had been aimed at Johnson’s train.

Clarke said: “The operation to attack this particular train will have been approved at the highest level.



“This would not have happened unless the Kremlin intended it to happen.”

Putin’s Security Council deputy Dmitry Medvedev had hinted about Moscow targeting such trains in a sinister threat just days earlier.

The former Russian President branded European leaders “terrorist sponsors” for their support of Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky and vowed “retribution”.

Medvedev tied up his warning with the chilling message: “And they often travel to Kyiv by train…”

No casualties were reported in the attack, but the strike has sparked fears about Putin’s spiralling aggression towards Europe.



Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said that Russian strikes were hitting closer to NATO and EU member Poland.

“Putin’s terror is literally knocking on the doors of the European Union and NATO,” he said.

Putin is desperately trying to thwart European support of Ukraine as he prepares to strike Ukraine in the deadliest winter blitz yet.



Russia and the UK are at loggerheads after Andy Burnham‘s agreed to give Zelensky blueprints for long-range Storm Shadow missiles, angering the Kremlin.

Asked how Russia will respond – and whether it is weighing up strikes on British territory – the Russian president said: “That’s a secret, a military secret”.

He added that “any military facilities in Ukraine are our legitimate target, British or otherwise”.

Clarke said: “We are certainly heading for a militarised confrontation with Russia either this year or next year for sure.

“That confrontation may well come at sea. It might come in the air shooting Russian drones down, maybe even Russian aircraft who are moving into our airspace.



“We are going to have to be prepared to bring down drones.”

Following the rail attack, the EU’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accused Russia of attempting to scare Western countries with the attack.

Both Ukrainian and Polish authorities said the Russian drone struck 2km (1.2 miles) from the Polish border when it struck the passenger train on Sunday.



In Poland, Prime Minister Donald Tusk held an emergency meeting to discuss the Russian “escalation” creeping “closer and closer to our border”.

US intelligence officials have been warning of an imminent Russian incursion into Polish territory to test Nato’s defences for months.

Moscow has been widely accused of waging hybrid attacks across Europe.

This includes explosive-filled drones found at Leipzig Airport, an arson attack on a Ukrainian-owned drone manufacturer in Slovakia, and a huge blaze at a defence firm warehouse in Bulgaria, all in the past month.

Clarke said: “In the next couple of weeks, we will see whether Russia is prepared to take some sort of action in the Baltic states or against Poland.



“They are building up to something, whether to frighten everybody or whether to really do it. We don’t know.

“But there are a lot of indicators that the Russians are preparing some sort of military initiative.”

Just last week Nato fighter jets were scrambled over Estonia after several drones were spotted in the Baltic nation’s airspace.



The UK stations a rapid response force of more than 1,000 troops equipped with high-tech military gear in Estonia.

In July the Ministry of Defence announced a new UK-Estonia defence roadmap to deepen military cooperation and strengthen NATO’s eastern flank.

Clarke said: “Estonia is the most vulnerable of all of the three Baltic states.

“An attack on Estonia in the next couple of months is entirely plausible and the forces there are on full alert for it.

“So we’re building up to some sort of military confrontation, and how that confrontation is handled will determine the bigger question as to whether we find ourselves sliding into a war with Russia.”



For years, NATO countries have watched Russian drones breach their airspace, reluctant to shoot them down for fear of escalation.

But Ukraine’s allies must now respond with force to deter Putin before a direct attack on Europe, Clarke said.

He warned: “In the past it’s been a series of condemnations and increasing sanctions.

“But we are reaching the point where we’re going to have to be more muscular.

“Unless we’re prepared to keep backing down this war is going to get more dangerous before it is over.”



It comes as Putin prepares for his deadliest winter blitz yet against Ukraine.

Last month the Russian despot said Russia’s military had been “ordered to prepare and carry out mass strikes” on Ukraine’s energy facilities.

And as Russia steps up its production of ballistic missiles – now at a rate of more than 100 a month – Kyiv’s supplies of interceptors have tumbled.



Ukraine is trying to get an additional 300 Patriot missiles from its partners this winter, but there is no guarantee.

Clarke said: “The Ukrainians desperately need air defences because they’re now up against a much more sophisticated Russian drone threats.

“They’ve got a long, hard winter coming where with the best will in the world, the technologies don’t exist in in enough form.

“There aren’t enough of them to actually give Ukraine the sort of air defense they’re going to need.

“And Putin is about to throw the kitchen sink at Ukraine for the next six months or so over the winter.”



Desperate Putin is expanding his drone network as he prepares to take on the West to deter support reaching Ukraine.

Moscow has started to deploy a high-speed jet variant of its Iranian Shahed drone model – capable of reaching targets almost 620 miles away.

Named Geran-4 and Geran-5, the UAVs can evade air defence systems while carrying a 90kg payload, according to Ukrainian government documents leaked online.

These will be launched alongside another 10,000 cheap Banderol cruise missiles during 2027.

Dozens of drone launch sites have emerged along Russia’s border – placing Nato allies well within reach of the dictator’s war machine.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Images showed enough storage at one base for more than 1,000 drones to be kept on site at one time.

Missiles launched from the secret sites could reach Nato territory with “the greatest of ease”, European affairs expert, Professor Anthony Glees previously told The Sun.

News.title: Husband in his 60s pleads guilty to drugging and raping his unconscious wife since early 2000s
News.content:
RAPE TRIAL Husband in his 60s pleads guilty to drugging and raping his unconscious wife since early 2000s

A HUSBAND in his 60s has pleaded guilty to drugging and raping his wife without her knowledge over a period of more than two decades, a court heard.

The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife’s legal right to anonymity, appeared at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court today where he admitted over 60 charges.

The man sobbed in the dock as he gave guilty pleas to dozens of charges of rape, assault by penetration, sexual assault and attempted rapes.

He also admitted administering a substance “with the intention of stupefying or overpowering” her “so as to enable” his wife to engage in sexual activity between November 2004 and October 2025.





The husband also admitted a further charge of sharing intimate pictures or video footage.

He pleaded guilty to eight more charges of serious sexual assault.

Earlier this year he pleaded guilty to various sexual offences against his wife on dates between 2022 and 2025 including rape and sexual assault.

His wife sat in the front row of the public gallery at Manchester’s Minshull Street Crown Court with her two adult children as he entered his guilty pleas over 18 minutes.



She watched intently, holding her children’s hands as her husband admitted his crimes, before dabbing her eyes.

The husband, who is a grandparent and held down a respectable job prior to being arrested, had already admitted 15 of the charges at an earlier hearing but was due to face trial for the other 45 counts.

The offending was carried out at the couple’s home in Stockport, Greater Manchester, prior to his shock arrest in October 2025.

The shocking case involves 13 other men who are alleged to have sexually abused the victim or helped supply substances to render her unconscious.



The other men are accused of joining in the abuse between September 2018 until November 2025 – when the arrests were made.

The husband and 12 of the 13 other men are currently standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court.

They are aged between 29 and 74 and include an ambulance paramedic once pictured meeting Prince Harry during a royal visit.

Also among them are a former nightclub DJ, a football club chief executive and university technician.

Twelve of them have denied a range of offences including rape, conspiracy to rape, assault by penetration, sexual assault and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent.



One has pleaded guilty to charges including conspiracy to rape.

Among them is an ambulance paramedic, a pensioner, a former DJ, a dog walker, a football coach and a taxi driver.

Others include a factory worker, an unemployed man and a former non-league football club chief exec.

Keith Fotheringham, 59, pleaded guilty in February 2026 to four offences between 2023 and 2025: conspiracy to rape, conspiracy to commit assault by penetration, conspiracy to administer a substance with intent and assault by penetration.

The married dad of two is a technician at the University of Dundee and lives in the Scottish city.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A jury of nine women and three men were formally sworn in earlier.

The trial is estimated to last for about 15 weeks.

News.title: Dad mauled by shark as beast ‘rips off his foot’ in savage attack while surfing alone off popular beach
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SHARK ATTACK Dad mauled by shark as beast ‘rips off his foot’ in savage attack while surfing alone off popular beach

A DAD has been mauled by a shark with the predator reportedly ripping off his foot in a savage attack off a popular beach.

Mel Ismail was surfing alone when he was attacked at Glenfield Beach in Geraldton, 267 miles (430km) north of Perth.



Luckily, teenagers on the beach in Australia used a surfboard rope to create a makeshift tourniquet to save his life.

Another surfer saw Ismail in distress surrounded by a pool of blood in the water and paddled out to bring him to shore.



The deep-sea beast bit a huge chunk out of his surfboard.

Ismail lost his foot in the attack, though the full extent of his leg injuries remain unclear, 9News reports.

Authorities have taken Ismail’s board and wetsuit to establish the species of shark behind the attack.

A large section of the Glenfield beach was temporarily closed after the shark attack on Monday, the City of Greater Geraldton announced.



“To ensure community safety all recreational water users are advised to avoid the area as the shark may still be in the vicinity,” the council said.

Signs were displayed on the sand warning that a shark had been sighted in the area.

St John Ambulance said a man in his 50s had been taken to Geraldton Hospital as a “priority one” emergency.

A WA Country Health spokesperson said the man was in a serious but stable condition.

The horror mauling follows a spate of shark attacks in Australia this year.



Leah Stewart, 34, was savaged by a shark while swimming at Coogee Beach in Sydney in June.

The attack left her in a coma for two weeks and her arm was so damaged it had to be amputated.

There four attacks in just two days in January, including a 12-year-old boy who died from his injuries.

A man was killed by a shark in Queensland in May.

News.title: Double killer Simon Levy denies stabbing prison guard in neck with pen before trying to strangle him in jail attack
News.content:
JAIL HORROR Double killer Simon Levy denies stabbing prison guard in neck with pen before trying to strangle him in jail attack

A CONVICTED double killer has denied that he stabbed a prison guard in the neck with a pen and tried to strangle him in a jail attack, a court heard.

Simon Levy, 41, is currently serving a whole life sentence for murdering two women in Tottenham, London.



Levy was also accused of ambushing Paul Dunne at maximum security HMP Belmarsh in February.

The 41-year-old was being held on remand at the time for murdering two women and raping a third in a crime spree in London.



Levy has been charged with assault occasioning actual bodily harm and intentional strangulation in an incident at HMP Belmarsh.

At a hearing at Woolwich Crown Court, sitting in the Royal Courts of Justice, on Monday, Levy appeared over a videolink from HMP Belmarsh.



The convicted killer, wearing grey prison issue clothes and sunglasses over his eyes, entered not guilty pleas to both charges

Judge Charlotte Welsh ordered Levy to stand trial on February 15 next year, in a case which is due to last up to four days.



At the first hearing of the case last month, prosecutor David Burns told the court Levy was finishing a meeting with Belmarsh guard Dunne when it is said he “attacked him with a pen, stabbing him multiple times to the arm and neck”.

It is said that Mr Dunne fell to the floor and Levy then “grabbed the officer around the throat” before allegedly tightening his grip.

Levy indicated during his first appearance in the magistrates’ court that he intends to fight the allegations of attacking Mr Dunne.

Judge Welsh adjourned the case for a further hearing on November 13, and set a pre-trial review hearing for January 19 next year.

Levy was handed a whole life term last month for murdering grandmother Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53, and mother-of-four Sheryl Wilkins, 39.



Carmenza was found dumped in the stairwell of a derelict building in Peckham, South East London, on March 17 last year.

Five months later, Levy murdered 39-year-old Sheryl amid a string of missed chances to stop him.

Sheryl was found collapsed near High Road, Tottenham, at 6.30am on August 24 last year.

The killings happened after he had also carried out a string of sexual assaults on the Tube and raped a woman in a car park.

Levy had been arrested three times by the British Transport Police but was granted bail each time.



The Crown Prosecution Service also failed to apply for an arrest warrant just 13 days before Sheryl’s death when he failed to attend court after his lawyers said he had a mental health issue.

News.title: Terrifying moment Brit tourists flee wildfires on little boats in Dunkirk-style evacuation from holiday island inferno
News.content:
SHOCKING images show scores of terrified British tourists fleeing wildfires tearing through a Croatian holiday island in a dramatic Dunkirk-style little boat evacuation.

Brits being showered with burning embers leapt into the sea after local hotel staff abandoned them at the Gava Waterman Milna Resort on the island of Brac.



They were only saved by a flotilla of around 50 local boats steered to the island as a wall of flames closed in.

Tourists told last night how they were left “surrounded by fire” and screaming as they jumped into the sea to escape the inferno.



They had earlier been assured there was no danger and told to go to their rooms and “relax with a drink” by reception staff alleged to have vanished as flames engulfed the resort’s perimeter.

Josh Robbins, a 26-year-old mortgage advisor on a romantic break at the woodland retreat with his fiancee Shelby A’Court (ckd) said: “It was terrifying.



“We were left to run for our lives as a wall of flames closed in as we were showered by burning embers.

“If we had stayed put as we were, people would have died and we were only saved by the little boats – it was like Dunkirk.”



Forest fires are believed to have been triggered by lightning strikes in tinder dry woodland on Thursday and began spreading towards Milna in the east of Brac on Friday.

Around a third of around 500 guests were Brits in 139 rooms and 17 low-rise woodland cottages at the Gava Waterman resort.

Trippers were first alerted by the arrival of firefighting sea planes drafted in to battle the wildfires on Friday then noticed smoke as the wind turned towards them.



Staff issued no warnings and insisted there was no danger as flames closed in on Saturday afternoon.

Worried trippers were told they were safe but advised to stay in their rooms as online maps showed the fire closing on Saturday night as the site was showered with ash.

Power was then cut to the entire resort at 9.35pm before trees and woodland around the resort were seen in flames and panicking trippers – including disabled pensioners – began to flee.

But they found reception staff had fled in their cars and were given no evacuation plan – and found the hotel main doors locked shut as the flames swept closer.

Brit tripper Josh told The Sun: “The staff had gone and we couldn’t get out because the sliding glass doors were locked shut – we thought we were going to die.



“There were dozens of people all trying to get out and we eventually had to prize the doors open to escape.

“The reception staff had driven off down the resort’s narrow access road but their cars had blocked the route stopping fire appliances reaching us.

“When we got outside the car park was surrounded by a wall of fire as firefighters tried to hold back the flames.



“We realised fire was about to engulf the hotel and decided to run down the path to the wooden dock to the sea to escape. “

Holidaymakers struggled down the unlit steps to the dock in total darkness using only their mobile phone torches after grabbing passports and leaving luggage in their rooms.

Josh’s partner Shelby, an IT compliance officer, told The Sun: “It was chaos. I saw a disabled person crying in a wheelchair because they couldn’t get away.

“A British woman fell into the sea at the dockside and it took three or four of us to get her out.

“Flames were closing in all around and people started jumping into the water when we started getting showered with hot embers.



“Myself and Josh eventually grabbed a paddle board and just clung to it as people screaming and panicked all around us.

“No one told us where to go or what to do – until we saw local boats arriving to save us.

“We ended up using our arms and legs to swim the paddle board to one of the boats and were absolutely exhausted when we reached it.



“Josh lost his shoes as we swam and I have to abandon stuff in my bag because it was soaked through and dragging me down.

“Others swam for it and it’s amazing no one was lost or drowned in the darkness – and someone would be held accountable for this.”

Steve Saunders, a 57-year-old electrician from Rainham, Kent who was at the resort with his wife Anna, 52, said: “Anna was supposed to be celebrating her birthday this weekend but we ended up running for our lives.

“If we’d stayed in the hotel we could have been choked by smoke or caught in the fire – the woodland cottages at the resort were wiped out.

“It was a huge relief to reach one of the boats which came to save us but I can’t believe we were abandoned and given no instructions whatsoever.”



British tripper Lorraine Pearce said in a Facebook post: “There was no evacuation plan – we all just ran.

“A couple of guests operated the hoses to keep the path to the beach clear for guests to escape …absolute heroes.

“Local people were amazing, giving us clothes and blankets offering us rooms to stay. Also local people coming out on their boats. Thank you so much.



“All guests worked together and we have made friends for life through this.

“But why did we not get an alarm until we were in rescue boats?”

Gave resort guest Debbie King said in another post: “Even before the firefighters arrived the reception area had been deserted by staff. No evacuation instructions were given.

“My praise goes out to the firefighters, life boat crews and locals who made the evacuation possible.”

Rescued Brits Josh, Shelby, Steve and Anna were among a group of eight pals on an £1,800-a-week all-inclusive TUI package trip to the resort, which also hosts Brits on Jet2, Saga and EasyJet trips.



Rescued Brits were ferried to hotels in the Croatian coastal city of Split and were awaiting flights home last night and no injuries were reported in the evacuation.

Small craft including speedboats and fishing vessels sped to their aid after a general alarm was issued.

Little boats from England saved more than 300,000 Allied soldiers trapped by advancing German forces in northern France during the Dunkirk evacuation during World War II.



A TUI spokeswoman said yesterday: “This is obviously not the kind of experience we want our guests to have on holiday.

“We’re making inquiries and looking into what happened.”

The Gava Waterman resort was approached for comment.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A TUI spokeswoman added: “We know this will have been a distressing experience for those affected by the wildfire on the island of Brac.

“The safety of our customers is our highest priority and our local teams have been supporting those impacted and working closely with the hotel and local authorities”.

News.title: Three sisters seriously injured in M9 crash that killed five teens share ‘difficult’ update
News.content:
Three sisters seriously injured in M9 crash that killed five teens share ‘difficult’ update

Three sisters, aged in their 20s and 30s, and a young boy were left seriously injured when a car travelling the wrong way down the M9 in Co Kildare crashed into them

View 2 Images The scene of the crash on the M9 in Co Kildare (Image: Niall Carson/PA Wire)

Three sisters seriously injured in a car crash that killed five teenagers have shared an emotional update after describing the past few weeks as “incredibly difficult”.

‌



Sisters Ella Hendricken, Niamh Kinsella and Alma Kinsella, aged in their 20s and 30s, were travelling with a seven-year-old boy when a BMW being driven the wrong way down the M9 in Co Kildare hit their vehicle head-on in the early hours of August 16.

‌



The family had been heading to Dublin Airport for a holiday. The sisters said they are continuing to recover, are “getting stronger” and are taking things “one day at a time”.

‌



Five teenagers who were in the BMW died at the scene of the collision, with their funerals taking place in the days after the crash.

The teenagers were Alex McCarthy, 16, and Jeremy O'Brien, 18, both from Carlow, Joey Carthy, 15, and Jack Kennedy, 17, both from Athy, and Kamil Pustkowski, 17, who lived in Dublin and Limerick.

A GoFundMe launched by a friend of one of the injured women has so far raised over 820,000 euro (£700,000).

‌



View 2 Images L-R: Ella Hendricken, Niamh Kinsella and Alma Kinsella were injured in the crash

In a online post, the sisters said they wanted to share an update and thank the public as they revealed they were "getting stronger" each day.

"We are continuing to take things one day at a time and are getting stronger as the days go by," they said in a joint statement.

‌



"We're incredibly grateful for all the kindness, messages and support that have been shown to us and our family.

"The past few weeks have been incredibly difficult for all of us, but the support we’ve received from so many people has meant more than we could ever put into words.

"To every person who has donated, shared the fundraiser, sent a message or simply kept us and our family in your thoughts and prayers. Thank you.

Article continues below

"The generosity and kindness shown to us has been overwhelming, and we are incredibly grateful. For now, we're continuing to focus on getting stronger and taking each day as it comes.

"With all our thanks, Ella, Niamh and Alma."

The organiser of the GoFundMe page said all donations will be going directly to the family, who are facing a "long and challenging road ahead."

News.title: 'I live full-time in a hotel with my husband and two dogs — and the perks are great'
News.content:
'I live full-time in a hotel with my husband and two dogs — and the perks are great'

Lilli Holland has been living long-term in hotels for more than one year and says she particularly likes the housekeeping, and having a gym and swimming pool in the same building

View 6 Images Lilli Holland lives full-time in a hotel (Image: Jam Press/@_lillisinfo_)

A young woman who lives full-time in hotels with her husband and two dogs has told of the perks of this lifestyle.

‌



Lilli Holland, 22, has spent more than a year residing in accommodation with her husband because his job requires him to temporarily work in different locations, with his employer covering their accommodation. The couple can spend months at a time in the same hotel, with their current base in Florida having been their home since May.

‌



Lilli, a remote worker from Virginia, US, travels with her husband and their two dogs, Selina and Diana, allowing her to see more of the country while enjoying some unexpected perks of hotel life.

‌



Lilli, a private tutor, said: "There are definitely some benefits – free breakfasts being one. Until recently, I got breakfast from the hotel lobby every day. Now that I'm tracking what I eat more closely, I usually eat breakfast in our room, but I still go down to the lobby for my morning coffee."

6 View 6 Images Some hotels, including Lilli's current one, are self-catering (Image: Jam Press/@_lillisinfo_) 6 View 6 Images Lilli is able to get breakfast in the lobby and take it back to her room (Image: Jam Press/@_lillisinfo_)

‌



But food is not the only perk. Lilli said regular housekeeping was another major benefit, although the arrangements vary between hotels.

"From my understanding, this isn't every hotel, but at the hotels where we've had long-term stays, housekeeping has required access to the room at least once a week to make sure nothing is severely neglected or damaged," she said.

"I usually schedule two days a week when housekeeping can come during certain hours. They change the linens, vacuum, clean the bathroom and occasionally clean the kitchen."

‌



Because the couple travels with two dogs, Lilli said she tries to make things as easy as possible for hotel staff. Lilli, who has no children, added: "Before housekeeping comes, I also make sure our personal belongings are picked up and out of their way – they're there to clean the room, not organise or handle our stuff."

The couple have also made the most of the facilities available to them, with every hotel they have stayed in offering a gym, swimming pool and complimentary WiFi.

View 6 Images Lilli works remotely - so she can live in the hotel and operate as a private tutor online (Image: Jam Press/@_lillisinfo_)

‌



Lilli moved into hotels with her husband in June 2025 as part of his work as a military contractor for a private company. Since then, they have had one long-term stay in Maine before moving to their current base in Florida.

They try to make each hotel room feel more like home, putting up small decorations around holidays such as Thanksgiving. Where rooms do not have fully equipped kitchens, they have also improvised with an air fryer to prepare meals.

The unusual arrangement has allowed the couple to save thousands of dollars, as Lilli's husband's employer covers the cost of their accommodation. She estimates that renting a one-bedroom apartment in their home state would cost around $1,300 (£960) a month, with utilities adding up to another $300 (£220).

‌



However, Lilli stressed that living in a hotel would not necessarily be cheaper if they had to pay the full price themselves. She said: "We aren't choosing hotel living because it's cheaper than renting.

"If we were personally paying the normal hotel rate, it obviously wouldn't be. The discounted rate for our current stay works out to around $1,000 (£740) per week, although it varies. At the hotel's standard rate without his employer's discount, the same stay would cost around $1,800 (£1,300) per week."

6 View 6 Images Lilli's dogs live in the hotel room too, and the woman is able to walk them near her hotel (Image: Jam Press/@_lillisinfo_) 6 View 6 Images Lilli's current living space is in a hotel in Florida (Image: Jam Press/@_lillisinfo_)

‌



The couple are due to return temporarily to Virginia in October, where they can stay with family. For longer stays of several months, they instead use a furnished rental.

But despite the perks, Lilli admits that spending months at a time in a hotel can be difficult. She continued: "The biggest con to living in a hotel is simply that it isn't your home," she said.

"We have decorations, sentimental items and other belongings in storage back home that we can't display or use because we don't have space for them. It also makes having family visit more difficult.

‌



"We usually have a pull-out couch, but then our beds are essentially side-by-side in one room, which doesn't really work when my husband has to get up for work at 4 a.m. the next morning."

There are also practical challenges that only become apparent after months of living out of a hotel room.

"You have limited storage, limited kitchen space and very little separation between where you sleep, work, eat and relax. You have to get creative about making a relatively small space function as a home," Lilli said.

‌



Despite the drawbacks, however, the couple have no plans to give up their unusual lifestyle anytime soon.

"We plan to continue doing this for at least the next few years," Lilli said.

"My husband likes his job, and being able to travel was always a goal of mine, so right now this gives us a lot of the best of both worlds.

Article continues below

"We're young and don't have children, so it feels like a great time in our lives to take advantage of the opportunity, experience different places and eventually figure out where we'd like to settle more permanently.

"It was also always a goal of mine to travel, so it works really well for us at this point in our lives."

News.title: ‘Do not swim’ warning issued at Exmouth Beach after water turns bright blue
News.content:
‘Do not swim’ warning issued at Exmouth Beach after water turns bright blue

The Environment Agency warned visitors not to bathe at Exmouth Beach in Devon after pollution entered the nearby Littleham Brook, turning the water bright blue

View 3 Images Visitors were urged 'do not swim' (Image: Environment Agency)

A mystery substance that turned the water at a popular UK beauty spot bright blue has prompted an urgent "do not swim" warning for visitors.

‌



The Environment Agency (EA) has advised people not to bathe at Exmouth Beach in Devon after pollution entered nearby Littleham Brook, which flows into the sea.

‌



The source of the unusual blue pollution was traced back to an "industrial source" on Saturday night and the leak has since stopped. The agency added that there was no "visible environmental impacts".

‌



The warning comes after a separate sewage spill near Exmouth's bathing waters earlier this week, although the two incidents are not linked.

View 3 Images Littleham Brook flows into the sea at Exmouth Beach (file) (Image: Getty Images)

The pollution at Littleham Brook is thought to have appeared just after 8:30pm on September 11.

‌



As a precaution, swimmers have been advised against entering the water at Exmouth beach as the water is analysed for toxicity, the EA said.

"A bright blue substance was reported in Littleham Brook, Exmouth," a spokesperson said in a post on X. "We attended and found no visible environmental impacts, but issued an advice against bathing as a precaution.

"Overnight it was traced to an industrial source, but it has stopped. It is not linked to the sewage network.

‌



"The pollutant is still moving downstream and is likely to reach the bathing water this afternoon.

View 3 Images The water at Littleham Brook turned bright blue (Image: Environment Agency)

"We're awaiting toxicity information, so the advice against bathing on Swimfo remains. We'll review again later and lift it when safe."

Article continues below

The EA further explained its restrictions on its interactive bathing quality map, adding: "Exmouth bathing water is affected by the catchment surrounding the Littleham Brook, which is approximately 600 hectares, and also by the enormous Exe Estuary catchment which is approximately 150,000 hectares.

"The Littleham Brook is four and a half kilometres long and flows southwest from Littleham Village through Green Farm and Maer Farm to Maer Bridge where it is piped under the beach to the sea at Maer Rocks."

News.title: Double murderer Simon Levy faces trial accused of stabbing prison guard in neck with pen
News.content:
Double murderer Simon Levy faces trial accused of stabbing prison guard in neck with pen

Double killer Simon Levy has denied allegations that he stabbed a Belmarsh prison guard in the neck with a pen and then tried to strangle him during an incident in February

View 2 Images Simon Levy murdered two women in Tottenham in 2025 (Image: Metropolitan Police/PA Wire)

Double killer Simon Levy will stand trial next year over allegations that he stabbed a prison guard in the neck with a pen and attempted to strangle him.

The 41-year-old, who is serving a whole-life sentence for murdering two women in Tottenham, has been charged with assault occasioning actual bodily harm and intentional strangulation following an incident at HMP Belmarsh in February.

Appearing by videolink from Belmarsh, Levy entered not guilty pleas to both charges at Woolwich Crown Court, which was sitting at the Royal Courts of Justice, on Monday.

Judge Charlotte Welsh ordered Levy to stand trial on February 15 next year, with the case expected to last up to four days.

View 2 Images Levy is serving a whole-life order at HMP Belmarsh (Image: Getty Images)

At the first hearing of the case last month, prosecutor David Burns told the court Levy was finishing a meeting with Belmarsh guard Paul Dunne when he is alleged to have "attacked him with a pen, stabbing him multiple times to the arm and neck".

Mr Dunne is said to have fallen to the floor, after which Levy is alleged to have "grabbed the officer around the throat" before tightening his grip.

The incident happened on February 18, when Levy was being held on remand at the maximum-security prison.

He indicated during his first appearance at Westminster Magistrates' Court that he intends to contest the allegations that he attacked Mr Dunne.

Levy, formerly of Tottenham, north London, was handed a whole-life order in August for murdering grandmother Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53, and mother-of-four Sheryl Wilkins, 39, last year.

The killings happened after he had raped a woman in a car park and carried out a string of sexual assaults on the Tube.

Judge Welsh adjourned the case for a further hearing on November 13 and set a pre-trial review hearing for January 19 next year.

News.title: Dead body visible from public footpath after staff at NHS' Worthing Hospital propped open fire door
News.content:
Dead body visible from public footpath after staff at NHS' Worthing Hospital propped open fire door

Human Tissue Authority (HTA) inspectors who visited NHS' Worthing Hospital in West Sussex saw a body being prepared for release from a publicly accessible area

View 2 Images Worthing Hospital, which is in West Sussex, has been reprimanded (Image: Daily Mirror)

A dead body in a hospital mortuary was visible from a public footpath after staff left a fire exit propped open during hot weather, inspectors have found.

‌



Human Tissue Authority (HTA) inspectors made the disturbing discovery during an inspection of Worthing Hospital in West Sussex on July 7 and 8, amid a heatwave. They found the mortuary office fire exit was "frequently opened" during periods of hot weather, providing what they described as unrestricted access to the body store.

‌



Inspectors also warned that when the doors were propped open, there was a direct line of sight from a publicly accessible footpath into the mortuary.

‌



Although the path at the rear of the hospital was not frequently used, inspectors said they were able to see a body being prepared for release while standing in the public area.

Dad given hours to live after pub roast dinner leaves him fighting for life READ MORE :

View 2 Images The hospital has an A&E department and approximately 500 inpatient beds (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

The HTA report said: “Although the footpath is located at the rear of the hospital and is not frequently used, during the inspection the inspection team was able to observe a body being prepared for release from this publicly accessible area.”

‌



The findings come amid growing warnings that the NHS must prepare for increasing pressures during the summer months, as well as winter.

Many NHS buildings are understood to be poorly equipped to cope with prolonged periods of hot weather, with some lacking adequate air conditioning.

Inspectors also found that CCTV covering the mortuary office fire exit was “not operational”, despite cameras being installed at the hospital.

‌



The security concerns are particularly serious in the wake of the David Fuller scandal, which saw the former hospital electrician abuse at least 100 dead women and girls in mortuaries across hospitals in the Southeast of England.

Following the scandal, NHS trusts were told to ensure access points to mortuaries and body stores were protected by swipe-card security and that effective CCTV was in place to monitor access to and from the areas.

During the inspection of Worthing Hospital and satellite sites at St Richard’s Hospital in Chichester and Royal Sussex County Hospital in Brighton, HTA officials identified 10 major and six minor breaches of its standards.

‌



All three sites are run by University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust.

A trust spokesperson told the Health Service Journal, which first reported the HTA findings, that the inspection had “identified areas where our standards needed to improve”.

They added that most of the issues had since been fully addressed.

Article continues below

A University Hospitals Sussex spokesperson said: "The dignity, security, privacy and respectful care of people after death are of fundamental importance to us, and we take the findings of the Human Tissue Authority (HTA) extremely seriously, including the areas identified by the inspection where our standards needed to improve.

“The vast majority of the areas identified in July have already been addressed, including all aspects of processes and procedures where inspectors identified any potential risk of error. We have also made immediate improvements to strengthen security and privacy, alongside a number of other changes to the physical environment, and more widely the Trust has already begun a far-reaching programme of improving all mortuary facilities across our hospital sites.

“The Human Tissue Authority has not suspended or revoked the Trust’s licence, and we continue to work closely with the regulator to ensure the highest standards of care, dignity and respect for deceased patients and their families.”

News.title: Private jet carrying singer and 7 others crash-lands in Brazil and bursts into flames
News.content:
Private jet carrying singer and 7 others crash-lands in Brazil and bursts into flames

Singer Rey Vaqueiro, real name David Linhares Pereira de Sousa, was taken to hospital alongside his team and crew members after their aircraft was consumed by flames in Brazil

Private jet carrying singer in flames after running off runway

A private jet carrying a singer on his way to a performance along with seven other people burst into flames after running off the runway.

‌



The crash-landing took place in Brazil in the early hours of Sunday at an airfield in Parelhas, Brazil, belonging to a mining company.

‌



Singer Rey Vaqueiro had been due to perform at the rural settlement. The pilot, co-pilot, Rey and the five other people on board the private jet managed to escape the aircraft before the fire spread.

‌



Nobody was injured, however the aircraft - a Cessna 550 Bravo - was destroyed in the blaze. Rey, 26, had performed in Moreno hours earlier and was due to perform in Parelhas at 2.30am.

View 3 Images The plane burst into flames after running off the runway (Image: Jam Press/FL360aero)

Plane crashes into field in Rhineland as cops confirm everyone on board is dead READ MORE :

Private jet explodes into flames during crash-landing as flights grounded in Libya READ MORE :

Both of the aircraft’s engines caught fire in the accident, with firefighters spending a total of five hours tackling the blaze. The Fire Department said: “Firefighters tackled the blaze and cooled the engines while the remaining fuel burned off.”

‌



The runway reportedly had no problems, and the aircraft’s airworthiness certificate was valid.

View 3 Images Rey Vaqueiro sings traditional music from rural north-eastern Brazil (Image: Jam Press)

The singer, whose real name is David Linhares Pereira de Sousa, his team and the crew were taken to a local hospital for medical checks and are said to be doing well. Minutes earlier, another aircraft carrying other members of Rey’s team had landed without incident.

‌



The performer is from São Paulo but sings traditional music from rural north-eastern Brazil. His schedule for this month included 33 shows and just four days off.

View 3 Images Emergency services at the scene (Image: Jam Press/FL360aero)

His 2025 song “Body Splash” has 19m views on YouTube.

Article continues below

Because of the accident, Rey cancelled his shows scheduled for Sunday in Custódia and Canhotinho.

CENIPA, Brazil’s aviation accident investigation agency, will investigate the accident

News.title: NHS 'serious' reminder about condition that 'needs urgent hospital treatment'
News.content:
NHS 'serious' reminder about condition that 'needs urgent hospital treatment'

People should get to hopsital if they have any warning signs as this issue

View 2 Images The NHS alert was shared on social media (Image: Mike Kemp/In Pictures via Getty Images)

People should be aware of the key warning signs of a common yet potentially deadly medical condition that can affect almost anyone. "Immediate medical help" will be needed if you spot certain red flags of sepsis, according to the NHS.

‌



Posting on Instagram in a new update, the health service wrote: "Sepsis is a life-threatening reaction to an infection which needs urgent treatment in hospital. It can be hard to spot. Make sure you know the symptoms, which can vary between adults and children."

‌



The post, which was sent out on World Sepsis Day, claims the condition is a "serious reaction that can be life-threatening". It is important for people to get "urgent treatment in hospital" as it can develop "very quickly".

‌



Old mice made to feel young again, a little stress is good for your cells, why you feel sleepy at 3pm, 'bad' cholesterol halved in one fell swoop - all this and more in our science newsletter

What is sepsis, and what are the warning signs?

According to the NHS website, sepsis is a serious reaction to an infection that can be life‑threatening. It can develop very quickly, sometimes over just a few hours, and needs urgent treatment in a hospital. If it is not treated, sepsis can progress to septic shock, which can be fatal in serious cases.

Symptoms present differently for adults, children and babies. It is important to know some of the clear signs - especially if a child is unable to tell you something feels wrong with their body

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The health service wrote: "A child or adult with sepsis might not have every symptom listed. Get immediate medical help if you or your child are unwell and you think there's something seriously wrong."

Noticing more subtle signs in babies and children, such as a rash that does not fade when you press it or them being sleepier than normal or difficult to wake, can help pin down the issue quickly. Children may also experience a seizure during a case of sepsis.

‌



Children and adults share symptoms such as not urinating all day or urinating very little, difficulty breathing (or breathing very fast), and a high or low temperature when you touch them. Adults may present with unique symptoms that are less common in children, such as confusion, slurred speech, and muscle pain.

View 2 Images You may need to call 999 (Image: Getty)

The exact cause of sepsis is not known, but it is thought that the immune system overreacts to an infection and begins damaging the body’s organs. The risk can also be affected by the type of infection, a person’s age, genetics, and any other health conditions they have.

Article continues below

Any type of infection can lead to sepsis, but bacterial infections, such as chest infections, are the most common cause. People have ended up with sepsis following other types of infection, like urinary tract infections (UTIs), abdominal infections such as appendicitis, and skin infections such as cellulitis or infected wounds.

Anyone can get sepsis, but there is a higher chance in babies under 12 months, adults over 75, and people who are pregnant or who have given birth, had an abortion or had a miscarriage in the past six weeks. The risk is also higher in people with weakened immune systems, such as those with conditions like HIV or sickle cell disease, those having chemotherapy, or those taking corticosteroids or immunosuppressants.

The UK Sepsis Trust provides help and support for anyone affected by sepsis, including family, friends and carers. Find more help and support online here.

News.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max biggest overhaul as one retailer cuts up to £815 off price
News.content:
iPhone 18 Pro Max biggest overhaul as one retailer cuts up to £815 off price

The latest iPhone models will be available to buy from Friday, September 18 - but Apple fans should move fast to secure theirs

View 2 Images The iPhone 18 models benefit from improved performance and extended battery life (Image: Apple)

Apple has unveiled its iPhone 18 line-up, including its most powerful models yet. Pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max opened on Saturday, September 12, with prices starting at £1,199 and £1,299 respectively.

Both models bring a number of upgrades over their predecessors, including an improved triple-lens camera system, the new A20 Pro chip and longer battery life. The unibody aluminium design remains largely unchanged and the choice of four on-trend colours are likely to appeal to Apple fans new and old.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will go on sale outright from Friday, September 18. But for eager Apple fans, pre-orders are now available through a number of retailers, with Sky offering some of the most competitive deals for pay monthly customers.



One of the most exciting features of both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max is major upgrades to the camera. Both feature a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, giving users more control over lighting, depth and detail when taking photos.

Both phones also benefit from improved performance and battery life, powered by Apple’s A20 Pro chip and a smaller Dynamic Island. The Pro Max goes a step further, offering the biggest battery life improvement yet seen on an iPhone.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max £45 Sky Mobile Buy Here Product Description Sky Mobile is offering Apple's iPhone 17 Pro from £45 per month with £12 upfront payment and a 3GB data plan.

They come in a choice of four stylish colours: black, silver, glacier (light blue) and new burgundy. To make it easier to stay organised on the go, the new iPhones also come with a redesigned Siri that features enhanced AI capabilities.

Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing, said: "With iPhone 18 Pro, we’ve made advancements to the areas our users care about most: camera, performance, battery, and intelligence. And we didn’t just make incremental improvements in these areas — we took huge leaps forward to create the best Pro iPhone we’ve ever made."

The Pro Max can last up to 29 hours on a single charge, while 15 minutes of fast charging can take the battery to around 50%. Its latest release comes in a choice of four colours - black, burgundy, glacier (light blue) and silver.

View 2 Images The iPhone 18 and iPhone 18 Pro Max feature an upgraded 48MP Fusion Main camera (Image: Apple)

Where to buy the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18 Pro Max

Buying the latest iPhone can be expensive, especially if you want one of the Pro models with all the newest features. But there are ways to keep the cost down, from choosing a cheaper contract to spreading the cost with a monthly payment plan and looking at trade-in deals.

Sky’s monthly payment option could be a more affordable way to spread the cost of the latest iPhone 18 Pro Max. Customers pay £12 upfront, followed by £45 a month, including the £41 phone payment and a £4-a-month 3GB data plan on a 36-month contract.

While the contracts run for 36 months, customers can upgrade to a new handset from 24 months at no additional cost as part of the optional Swap24 deal - a good value addition for customers who like to keep up with the latest tech. For those who'd rather buy the device outright, launch prices typically remain consistent across retailers, so expect major sellers like Amazon and Argos to match the £1,199 and £1,299 price points, respectively.
