View image in fullscreen Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw scored her third goal of the season at Aston Villa. Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters

Hills’ regret after red card

The Charlton manager, Karen Hills, said she was disappointed after the second-half red card for Ashleigh Neville against Everton led to a 1-0 defeat. Neville was sent off in the 58th minute for a high boot on Ruby Mace. While Hills suggested there was more hip-to-hip contact than anything else, she did not outright criticise the officials. “I don’t think the referee made the decision, it’s the fourth [official] and I guess they have to work together. Yes, her foot is a little bit high, but disappointed because that changes the game.” Charlton went down to nine players after Hawa Cissoko received two yellow cards in quick succession. Emillia Hawkins

View image in fullscreen Ashleigh Neville was sent off in the 58th minute for a high challenge. Photograph: Molly Darlington/WSL/Getty Images

Birmingham’s lack of WSL experience shows

On paper, Birmingham’s 2-2 draw against Brighton is an impressive feat for a promoted side, but the head coach, Amy Merricks, did not look too happy at the final whistle. Her team led the match by two goals with 15 minutes left to play, but Olivia Garcia got one back for Brighton in the 77th minute before Kiko Seike snatched a point with a last-gasp equaliser. The difference in experience between the two sides probably played a part in the later stages, with Birmingham in the WSL for the first time since 2022. “We’ll take a massive lesson today from those dying moments and how we see that out a bit better,” said Merricks. “What we can’t question is this group’s application and intent. They were on the front foot, they were tenacious. We look improved from last week, which, for me, is brilliant. We’re going to go up a notch because I know this team, they won’t settle, they’re very hungry.” EH

Sports.title: Ludek Miklosko, former West Ham and QPR goalkeeper, dies aged 64
Sports.content:
The former West Ham and QPR goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko has died at the age of 64. Miklosko, who won caps for Czechoslovakia and Czechia, had cancer.

Miklosko joined West Ham from Baník Ostrava in 1990 for £300,000 after a trial and helped the club win promotion to the top division in his first season. He left in 1998 having made 373 appearances, joining QPR, initially on loan. Miklosko ended his career there in 2001 and returned to West Ham, where he worked as a goalkeeping coach until 2010.

He later worked for a sports agency before taking roles at Baník Ostrava as a board member and sporting director.

View image in fullscreen Ludek Miklosko made 373 appearances for West Ham. Photograph: Tony Marshall/Empics Sport/PA Images/Alamy

West Ham said Miklosko would “for ever hold a special place in the hearts of the West Ham family”. The club described him as a “beloved, inspirational goalkeeper and gentle giant of a man”.

Miklosko played 40 times for Czechoslovakia and twice for Czechia in an international career that began in 1982. He said in 2024 that he was withdrawing from cancer treatment.

His son Martin Miklosko said in a statement shared by West Ham: “We are heartbroken at his loss, but take huge comfort from the immense support he received from all of you, along with the knowledge that he is now at peace and no longer suffering.

“Dad simply loved West Ham United, and especially hearing his name sung loud and proud at every game. The club, and its fans, were and always will be a part of our family, so thank you all from the bottom of our hearts.”

Sports.title: Top of the table, empty in the stands: inside the revolt against Lazio’s owner | Nicky Bandini
Sports.content:
Gennaro Gattuso has given some memorable post‑game interviews down the years. Who could forget his “sometimes maybe good, sometimes maybe shit” rant at OFI Crete or the face of the beleaguered interpreter tasked with translating it?

Last year, not long before taking charge of the Italian national team, Gattuso got into a finger‑jabbing, language‑swapping, almost‑nose‑to‑nose shouting match with Josko Jelicic on Croatian television.

There was something more affecting about the soft way he spoke in his Calabrian accent on Saturday. Without anger, but with an air of melancholy. “Football without fans is shit,” he said. “What do you think? I’d say it’s better to stay home. Better to go for a walk with the dogs.”

He had just seen his Lazio side let a two-goal lead slip at home against Milan, but that was hardly a disaster. The Biancocelesti are still top of the table, at least until Roma and Inter play on Monday. For a team who lost several starters in the summer, who began his tenure with a cup defeat by a Serie B club in August and whose fans refuse to enter their own stadium, this season has already exceeded expectations.

It may represent the beginnings of a redemption arc for Gattuso, who stood down from managing Italy in April after failing to qualify for the World Cup. He was not a popular choice to succeed Maurizio Sarri in Rome.

He is not the reason why supporters are boycotting Lazio’s home games in huge numbers. Season ticket sales have fallen from close to 30,000 last year to less than 4,500, according to the football finances website Calcio e Finanza. Last season’s home game against Milan drew 50,000 spectators, but the same fixture on Saturday had less than half that number, with a noisy majority cheering for the visitors.

Lazio’s fans have not stopped caring. Hundreds gathered outside the team’s training ground before the game, forming a convoy of mopeds to escort the players’ bus to Ponte Milvio – a bridge that crosses the Tiber River close to the Stadio Olimpico. A statement released by supporters’ groups beforehand had announced their intention to go from there “to watch the game in a pub or at home”.

View image in fullscreen Gennaro Gattuso said that football means very little without fans. Photograph: Alessandra Tarantino/AP

It is an act of protest specifically against the club’s owner, Claudio Lotito. Fans have travelled in their thousands to away games, even for unglamorous pre-season friendlies, reinforcing the message that they still care about their club, but do not want to endorse the man who controls it.

The feud with Lotito is not new. In January, an open letter was posted on Change.org accusing him of denying fans the right to dream throughout his more than two decades as owner. “It has been years, almost seven, since we lifted a trophy,” reads the petition, signed by more than 45,000. “These are years in which we have not signed a footballer to stir the heart of fans young and old.”

Quick Guide Serie A results Show Venezia 2-4 Fiorentina Genoa 1-1 Frosinone Lazio 2-2 Milan Atalanta 1-2 Cagliari Lecce 3-2 Monza Napoli 1-0 Bologna Sassuolo 3-2 Juventus Monday's fixtures: Como v Parma Torino v Roma Internazionale v Udinese Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

There are layers to these grievances. The letter references the club’s handling of a memorial for Vincenzo Paparelli, a Lazio supporter killed by a flare fired from the Roma end during a derby in 1979. Lotito was accused of denying Paparelli’s niece a chance to walk on to the pitch during an event last November.

He denied that version of events, saying “the real problem was that four representatives of the organised support wanted to go with her”.

Lotito has been accused of simply not paying attention to Lazio with his focus elsewhere. He is active in politics, having been elected to the Italian senate in 2022.

He bought another football club, Salernitana, in 2011, and over the next 10 years helped them to get promoted from Serie D to the top flight, at which point he was forced to sell up due to the conflict of interest. Rules have since been modified to prevent simultaneous ownership of two teams in the top three divisions, but that did not deter Lotito from completing the takeover of another fourth-tier club, Reggina, this summer.

Have such investments kept him from pursuing the big‑name signings Lazio fans crave? It is not exactly clearcut. Lazio could not have bought anyone last summer anyway, as they were placed under a transfer embargo for failing to meet liquidity requirements introduced by the Italian Football Federation. These, too, were the subject of debate as Lotito argued they failed to weigh the club’s successes in operating without major outstanding debts.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Diego Moreira scored the equaliser for the visitors in a stadium that felt like a Milan home game. Photograph: Giuseppe Cottini/AC Milan/Getty Images

Navigating those rules required selling a string of important players – Taty Castellanos and Mattéo Guendouzi in January, Mario Gila, Alessio Romagnoli and Ivan Provedel in the summer. But after the embargo was lifted, Lazio made some canny signings. The centre-back Danilho Doekhi arrived from Union Berlin on a free transfer, the striker Albert Gudmundsson came in on loan from Fiorentina, as did the midfielder Davide Frattesi from Inter.

The last of those looks like a steal, secured for a €5m (£4.28m) loan fee last month, with a right to buy for €10m next year. Frattesi cost Inter more than twice that much when they signed him off the back of a break-out season at Sassuolo in 2023, only to keep him for the next three years as understudy to Nicolò Barella, Hakan Calhanoglu and others in a stacked midfield.

After joining Lazio this summer, Frattesi – still just 26 – said he had deliberately chosen a club that would put the weight on his shoulders. He scored in his first three games: winners against Bologna and Genoa, then the opener in a 2-1 victory away against Udinese.

He did not find the net this weekend. Lazio’s best attacking work originated from Mattia Zaccagni on the left wing. He had a cross converted at the back post by Matteo Cancellieri in the 10th minute, then another forced home at the second attempt by Tijjani Noslin after a defender knocked it on to the crossbar. Zaccagni had a close-range attempt of his own well saved by Mike Maignan in-between. It could have been a rout. Instead, Milan made three half-time substitutions and one of them, the €50m signing Diego Moreira, scored a pair of fine goals to ensure the game finished 2-2.

Might things have gone differently in a stadium packed with Lazio supporters, instead of one that felt like Milan’s home away from home? “Maybe with our fans here we would have managed to hold out,” Zaccagni said. “But the draw is a fair result in the end.”

Gattuso thanked the fans who had come to show their support beforehand. “I don’t think anyone is happy with this situation,” he said. “Everyone wants to come to the stadium, to have 50,000 people, 55,000 people.

“I think those fans came [to the training ground] because they recognise what the players are giving them. The fact of not giving up. The fact they are wearing the shirt with pride. That’s my reading. And that made me emotional today, seeing the people who came. It’s not football without the fans.”

Sports.title: PSG have finally won a game in Ligue 1 – but they were far from convincing
Sports.content:
It was just a flicker. Ferran Torres picks the ball up and passes it to João Neves. The Portugal midfielder plays it into Ousmane Dembélé, who has lured in Raphaël Le Guen and eliminates him with a mesmeric first-time back-heel into the path of Torres.

The Brest defence are just cones in a training drill, mere extras in this work of art as the Spaniard glides back into the scene to pass the ball into Egil Selvik’s bottom-left corner from 25 yards; it happened in slow motion, but was too quick for the Norwegian goalkeeper to react.

It is a move that had the slick and elegant fluidity of what we have come to expect from Paris Saint-Germain. Just four minutes in, the champions were ahead and the Stade Francis Le-Blé anticipated a show of force, a statement from their visitors.

Luis Enrique had described PSG’s start to the Ligue 1 season as catastrophic. A comfortable 6-1 win against Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League last Wednesday signalled a welcome return to form. The Sopposition manager, none other than Yaya Touré, described his opponents on the night as a machine – we have heard that before.

But once again, PSG were defective in Brittany on Sunday night, even if they did leave with all three points. Torres’s sublime finish was the only goal of the game. It was the Spaniard’s sixth since joining from Barcelona in the summer. All of his six efforts on target this season have found the net. He is clearly still riding the crest of a wave of confidence, having scored the winner in the World Cup final.

Torres’s supreme confidence is not shared by his teammates. Vitinha in particular has yet to resurface since the summer break and PSG are suffering from the lack of incision he usually provides. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is not quite back to his usual levels either and going into this game, there were creeping doubts about Matvey Safonov in goal. The Russian was at fault last weekend when Stanis Idumbo finished at his near post to secure a win for Monaco. It was at his near post he conceded to Kai Havertz in the Champions League final in May; if there is a weakness in PSG, Safonov was the most likely candidate.

But it is only thanks to him that PSG ended a run of five games without a win against French opponents. He was not forced into action when Nuno Mendes played Kamory Doumbia in one-on-one in the second half, the Mali international striking the outside of the PSG post.

Safonov did get a strong hand down low to his left when Doumbia rose highest to thunder a header towards goal and in the dying stages Pathé Mboup’s curled effort to the far post was tipped around the corner.

View image in fullscreen Goalkeeper Matvey Safonov kept PSG in the game with a number of saves. Photograph: Xavier Laine/Getty Images

Brest finished with a higher xG than the European champions, but had no points to show for it. Moments of brilliance in both areas were the difference. But that is what PSG are confined to at the minute: moments, flickers of brilliance.

“It was the worst of our four Ligue 1 matches, even if we won,” said Luis Enrique. “In the other three matches, we showed a high level at the back, but our opponents scored every chance. This time, it was the opposite.”

Alarm bells are not ringing. PSG often start slowly and it is only the quality of opposition faced at the start of the last campaign that ensured there was not such a significant deficit to the leaders. They are five points behind Lille, Monaco and Rennes, all of whom are on 10 points.

Last week, Marquinhos said that it was “a matter of ambition and motivation” as PSG hoped to replicate the success of the past two seasons. Just like Torres’s passed finish, PSG are all about timing and they have a knack for peaking at the right moment.

There were no doubts Brest were up to the occasion. The Stade Francis Le-Blé was a cauldron of emotion as Eric Roy was commemorated. The Brest manager, who guided the club into European competition for the first time, in 2024, died in June due to pancreatic cancer that began when he was appointed as the club’s manager in January 2023. His diagnosis was never made public.

Roy’s daughter, Victoria-Rose, spoke on the pitch before the match, “King Eric” shirts were worn on the sidelines and there were further moments of commemoration in the stands throughout the game. Hugo Magnetti said they had played for Roy. “He would have been proud of us, but he would have also ticked us off for missing some big chances.”

The game, at times, felt like a subplot, but what happened in it was not inconsequential. Some of those fears about waning “ambition and motivation” were deepened, as was a crisis of confidence among some of PSG’s key players, despite victory. But there were also flickers of brilliance Luis Enrique must hope will become more enduring as the season progresses.

Quick Guide Ligue 1 results Show Lille 2-0 Troyes Le Mans 2-2 Lens Brest 0-1 PSG Strasbourg 1-1 Monaco Auxerre 1-0 Nice Le Havre 0-0 Angers Lorient 2-2 Toulouse Paris FC 0-0 Lyon Rennes 1-0 Marseille Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

Will Still and Auxerre have their first points on the board thanks to their young English forward Cameron Archer. The Southampton loanee made his debut last weekend and scored a stunner in a 3-1 defeat to Lyon. This weekend he scored the only goal of the game against Nice. The win drags Auxerre off the bottom of the table – a place now occupied by their opponents on the day. Nice, without a win, have scored once in their first four matches. Their coach, Olivier Pantaloni, says there are traces of last season’s difficult campaign lingering in the minds of his players. They must quickly dispel them in order to avoid a repeat.

Four games in and the temperature is already rising in Marseille. The season started well, with a 4-0 home win to Strasbourg on opening day, but they have since lost to Monaco, Paris FC and Rennes. There is no real shame in any of those defeats; the matches were close and the opponents are expected to be in the race for Europe. “We can rival these teams but not yet beat them,” said Bruno Génésio after the 1-0 defeat at Rennes on Friday. Génésio added it was not up to him to state the club’s objectives this season – a clear message to his superiors. “We may need to explain things more clearly Maybe we have to say it so that people can understand.” The lack of quality and depth in the squad says enough; Marseille are outsiders in the race for European football.

This is an article by Get French Football News

Sports.title: Premier League LIVE: Gallagher says offside Haaland goal makes derby win ‘even better’, Pro Ref acknowledge mistake, Leeds vs Newcastle live
Sports.content:
Laur and order

Arsenal Invincible Lauren reveals the club's off the ball movement is one of the major reasons w

He said on the Sports Breakfast show: "They all know what to do in every single moment, if you have a look, most of the teams will press you high up.

"So nowadays, you have to identify where is the space, so the movement without the ball is key, because it's not like in our time [with] the pressing.

"The movement without the ball is key to build up from the back, it's key to getting the progression and being able to get into the latter third.

"When you have a look at the goals we scored against Chelsea, Chelsea sit back, have a look at the movement of our players, the speed of the situation of the ball and the movement without the ball.

"The movement is key, because you move and you're creating the spaces for your teammates, you allow your teammates to get into space and find the last pass and score the goal.

"We saw it against Chelsea, we saw it against Napoli with [Bruno] Guimaraes passing to Ben White, Ben White to [Martin] Odegaard, Odegaard to [Christos] Tzolis and Tzolis to Odegaard.

"You see the movement of the players without the ball, it was brilliant! We have scored since the beginning of the season 12 goals and conceded just one goal.

"It's due to the stability of the backline, the stability of the midfield and the movement to create the spaces in order to build up and finish chances in the last third, it's been absolutely brilliant."

Lauren continued: "If you have a look at Arsenal, we press up as a unit, the awareness of the backline to stay in the middle of the park, the midfield players [press] as well.

"We defend as a team, we attack as a team, so therefore we score so many goals and we just concede one goal, because it's due to the work of the whole team."

Sports.title: Thomas Frank and Match of the Day blasted for Tottenham ‘cop-out’ after Everton draw
Sports.content:
Thomas Frank and Match of the Day blasted for Tottenham ‘cop-out’ after Everton draw

Match of the Day fell below their high editorial standards as Thomas Frank offered no analysis on Tottenham Hotspur.

That's the view of talkSPORT host Paul Hawksbee in response to the former Spurs boss' lack of comments on the struggling side.



3 Spurs failed to find the back of the net for a fourth consecutive match on Saturday Credit: Getty

Frank was part of the Match of the Day panel on Saturday night with host Kelly Cates and ex-Premier League defender Ashley Williams.

The last set of highlights came from the 0-0 draw between Spurs and Everton, in which the former went goalless for a fourth straight league match at the start of a season for the first time ever.

Everton midfielder James Garner was selected as the standout player, with both Frank and Williams complimenting his performance at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.



But Frank, who was on the show seven months after being sacked by Spurs, did not assess the display shown by his former employers.

Hawksbee, a passionate Spurs fan, took issue with what he deemed to be a curious absence of punditry and revealed his belief that the Dane may have opted out of commenting on the club.



"There seemed to be a real odd abdication of responsibility on Match of the Day the other night," he said on Hawksbee and Jacobs.

"Thomas Frank was in the studio, and Tottenham v Everton was last. It wasn't a thriller, but there is a story there... it seemed to be the story everywhere else on planet Earth, that Tottenham haven't scored, another game they haven't scored.



"So what they did at the end of Match of the Day, was do an in-depth look at James Garner and his performance, and they never involved Thomas Frank at all.

"They just said to Ashley, 'James Garner was good, wasn't he?' He said, 'Yes, he was', and they showed a few bits.

"He did play well but (Jarrad) Branthwaite, I thought, was their best player, I thought he was brilliant. A, if you were going to single anybody out, it would have been him.

3 Frank was on punditry duty, but did not offer his view on Spurs' performance Credit: Getty



"And B, I just thought Thomas Frank had said, 'I don't want to talk about Spurs, especially the way it's going'... well, don't be a pundit then!

"I'm sure they will say that wasn't the case and they've been waiting for weeks to do the James Garner deep dive.

"I sat there and thought, 'Thomas Frank is on, I'd be interested to know what he says'. It was just a cop-out and, editorially, they're better than that."

What happened to Frank at Spurs?

A hugely successful spell at Brentford that included promotion to the Premier League boosted Frank towards a 'Big Six' job, which arrived at Spurs in June 2025.



He arrived as the successor to Ange Postecoglou, who just guided the club to their first trophy in 17 years by winning the Europa League.

However, Frank lasted just under eight months in the head coach role and was dismissed after a 2-1 home loss to Newcastle.

3 Frank was unable to last his first full season at Spurs Credit: Getty

The 52-year-old won just seven of his 26 league matches at Spurs and was winless across the last eight of his spell.



Spurs eventually finished 17th for a second consecutive season and only secured their survival on the final day.

Frank was later named as a pundit for the BBC during their coverage of the 2026 World Cup.

He was then announced as one of four new pundits on their famous Match of the Day show for the 2026/27 campaign.

Sports.title: Richarlison is eligible for Tottenham against Liverpool as Roberto De Zerbi confirms squad decision
Sports.content:
Richarlison is eligible for Tottenham against Liverpool as Roberto De Zerbi confirms squad decision

Richarlison's Tottenham Hotspur exile is set to continue.

Despite being left out of Spurs' 25-man squad for the Premier League, Richarlison is still eligible to feature in the Carabao Cup.

2 Richarlison's time at Spurs looks set to come to a sad end Credit: Getty

But Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi confirmed on Monday that the Brazilian forward would play no part in the club's Carabao Cup third round clash away against Liverpool on Tuesday evening, live on talkSPORT 2.

Roberto De Zerbi gives update on Richarlison's playing future

"Nothing has changed," De Zerbi said.

The Italian added: "I said last press conference. I know what happened in the last 45 days.

"It's not right if I explained. It's not my behaviour, the relationship.

"The problem is between the player and the club. I stay within the club. It's coach and club together.

"At the start of this season I spoke to him many times to convince him to stay and he didn't want to. I can't go every day to pray for him to stay."

Richarlison's difficult summer at a glance

Richarlison pushed to leave Spurs this summer and looked set to seal an emotional return to Everton on transfer deadline day.

However, the deal fell through.

Richarlison was then in talks to join Brazilian club Vasco da Gama but he failed to agree personal terms.

With Richarlison unable to secure an exit to date, it's left him in a tricky spot until January, when the transfer window re-opens.

2 De Zerbi looks prepared to make do without Spurs' top scorer from last season Credit: Getty

However, the 29-year-old has approached FIFA in an attempt to terminate his Spurs contract.

Should the case rule in his favour, Richarlison would then become a free agent, leaving him free to move wherever he chooses.

Richarlison's Tottenham career at a glance

Richarlison joined Spurs from Everton in July 2022 and has gone on to make over 130 appearances for the club.

In that time, the forward has registered 32 goals and 15 assists along with helping the club win the Europa League in 2025.

Richarlison finished as Spurs' top scorer last term, netting 12 goals across all competitions.

He has already featured once for the north London outfit this term, starting their Premier League season opener against Brentford.

Sports.title: Manchester United vs Brighton LIVE commentary: Carrick ‘doesn’t need break’ ahead of Carabao Cup clash
Sports.content:
Manchester United vs Brighton LIVE commentary: Carrick ‘doesn’t need break’ ahead of Carabao Cup clash

Manchester United entertain Brighton in an all-Premier League Carabao Cup third round tie on Wednesday, live on talkSPORT.

With both sides in Europe this season, this marks the start of their Carabao Cup campaign.



3 Michael Carrick will hope he can lead Man United to Carabao Cup success this season Credit: Getty

And they've made contrasting starts to the Premier League season, with Man United only winning one of their opening four games and Brighton in the top four.

United suffered a controversial home Manchester derby defeat to Manchester City on Sunday, while Brighton thumped Coventry 5-0 on the road.

The visitors have an excellent recent record away to United, too, winning on four of their last five trips in all competitions.



Man United vs Brighton: Date and how to follow

This Carabao Cup third round game will be played on Wednesday, September 16.

Kick-off is set for 8pm at Old Trafford, with talkSPORT bringing you live coverage.



Adrian Durham is your presenter, while commentary comes from Jim Proudfoot and ex-England defender Micky Gray.

3 Brighton have not gone beyond the fourth round of this competition since 1978 – can Fabian Hurzeler take them on a cup run this time around? Credit: Getty



Man United vs Brighton: Team news

Rotation is inevitable with this tie coming between Premier League fixtures for both teams.

United boss Michael Carrick could call upon the likes of Benjamin Sesko, who scored on his first start of the season in last week's Champions League win over Sabah

Andrey Santos hasn't started since the opening weekend of the campaign so will likely come in too.

Luke Shaw missed the Manchester derby and may not feature, while Wednesday likely comes too soon for Carlos Baleba to make his United debut after joining from Brighton last month.



As for the Seagulls, Fabian Hurzeler may use the game to give summer signings such as Promise David and Ibrahim Osman more minutes.

However, Hurzeler has less room for manoeuvre in terms of shaking things up – they have a lengthy injury list including the likes of Kaoru Mitoma and Mats Wieffer.

3 Canada World Cup star Promise David is on a season-long loan from Union Saint-Gilloise Credit: Getty

Man United vs Brighton: What's been said?

Speaking after Sunday's painful defeat, Carrick insisted there was no need for United to rip things up and start again.



"We don't need a break or a restart," he said. "We've just got to move on and start winning again."

Hurzeler, meanwhile, is staying grounded despite Brighton's emphatic victory last time out.

"We will always be the team who are very humble and don't take things for granted," he said.

The draw for the fourth round of the Carabao Cup will be made after Wednesday's game.

Sports.title: Edu lands surprise new job just a week after Nottingham Forest contract ripped up
Sports.content:
Edu lands surprise new job just a week after Nottingham Forest contract ripped up

Edu has been named as part of a new board of directors at Bulgarian champions Levski Sofia.

The former Arsenal sporting director officially left his role as head of global football at Nottingham Forest last week.

2 Edu left his role at Nottingham Forest last week and has now joined Levski Sofia Credit: Getty

He had held the position for just over a year, but in March, he was banished from the club by owner Evangelos Marinakis.

talkSPORT reported that Edu was facing a fight to save his job, with Marinakis underwhelmed with his impact.

And his exit, which was a long time coming, was confirmed on September 7, with the Brazilian departing Forest.

Edu's role also included working with Greek club Olympiakos and Portuguese outfit Rio Ave. Both of those clubs are also owned by Marinakis.

What is Edu's new job?

But now, just days after leaving his position, the 48-year-old has started a new job at an unexpected club.

He has joined the board of directors at Levski Sofia, who won the league title in Bulgaria last season.

His specific job title is yet to be revealed, but he was announced by the club to have joined alongside four others.

Daniel Borimirov, Claudio Prakownik, Felipe Berliner and Matthew Cherry have also been named on the board.

Edu could potentially become chairman or an executive director though, with elections being held imminently.

In their announcement, Levski Sofia wrote: "His experience in sports strategy, selection, talent development and organisational building will be an important asset for the club on its path to a sustainable and competitive football structure."

2 Edu has joined the Bulgarian champions in a surprise switch after leaving England Credit: Getty

Edu's next step

Edu started his directorial career in 2011, having had success on the pitch for Arsenal, being one of Arsene Wenger's 'Invincibles'.

He played 79 times in total for the Gunners, playing for Corinthians and Valencia too, also earning 16 caps for Brazil.

His first post-playing career role was with his old club in Brazil Corinthians, as he became their director of football 15 years ago.

Edu went on to work for Iran and Brazil before joining Arsenal in a brand new role in 2019.

He became their technical director and then their sporting director before leaving in 2024 and eventually joining Nottingham Forest.

That didn't work out though, and now he's become part of Levski Sofia's board in a surprise move.

Levski Sofia ended Ludogorets' domination in Bulgaria last season, winning the league to stop their rivals' 14-straight titles.

Sports.title: Liverpool vs Tottenham LIVE commentary: Iraola and De Zerbi in need of victory in blockbuster Carabao Cup clash
Sports.content:
Liverpool vs Tottenham LIVE commentary: Iraola and De Zerbi in need of victory in blockbuster Carabao Cup clash

Liverpool face Tottenham on Tuesday in the pick of the ties from the Carabao Cup third round, live on talkSPORT 2.

For the Reds, this is where their quest to lift the trophy for a record-extending 11th time begins.

4 Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first Carabao Cup game as Liverpool boss Credit: Getty

Spurs have already played one game in the competition, thrashing Charlton 5-1 in the second round to reach this stage.

And this clash could present the ideal opportunity for both sides to kickstart their seasons.

While Liverpool are still unbeaten under Andoni Iraola, they've been inconsistent so far, winning two and drawing three games in all competitions.

Spurs, meanwhile, haven't tasted victory aside from their triumph over Charlton – they've failed to win or score in any of their opening four Premier League matches.

Both teams enter this encounter having been held to 0-0 home draws at the weekend, Liverpool by Fulham and Spurs by Everton, setting an unwanted club record in the process.

Liverpool vs Tottenham: Date and how to follow

This Carabao Cup third round clash will be played on Tuesday, September 15.

Kick-off at Anfield is scheduled for 8pm, and talkSPORT 2 will bring you all the action live.

Ian Danter and former Liverpool midfielder Charlie Adam are your commentators.

4 Dominic Solanke was among Spurs' five goalscorers against Charlton in the second round Credit: AFP

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

The game will also be televised live on ITV1 and Sky Sports Main Event.

Liverpool vs Tottenham: Team news

Expect to see plenty of rotation from both managers as they prepare for their teams' second of three matches in the space of just over a week.

Iraola could give minutes to some of Liverpool's young prospects like midfielder Trey Nyoni and winger Lewis Koumas, both of whom have featured in the Premier League already this term.

However, in-form Cody Gakpo is a doubt after being forced off in the first half at the weekend.

4 Gakpo had to be substituted 30 minutes into Liverpool's draw with Fulham on Saturday Credit: Getty

Roberto De Zerbi, meanwhile, could hand a Spurs debut to summer arrival Martin Dubravka in goal, with James Maddison potentially in line to make his first start since returning from a knee injury at the back end of last season.

Destiny Udogie is back from injury and available, though Sandro Tonali, Pedro Porro and Dejan Kulsevski all miss out.

Richarlison, who was left out of Spurs' Premier League squad, is eligible but will not be involved, De Zerbi has confirmed.

Liverpool vs Tottenham: What has been said?

Iraola admitted during the build-up that he is still learning about the demands of the schedule on his players.

"There are players who play every three ⁠days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances don't change too much," he said at his press conference on Monday.

"There are other players where the risk is bigger and the ​performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level isn't affected."

That comes after De Zerbi highlighted a psychological issue with his team on Saturday but insisted they're capable of doing much better amid their slow start to the campaign.

4 De Zerbi has identified a 'mental block' holding Spurs back Credit: Getty

"There is a word in Italian – sbloccarsi – that literally translates as if we unblock ourselves," he said.

"[It is] a mental block because four games, no wins, no goals scored...it is tough for the players. The team is extremely strong, we can score goals and we can win games."
