Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal man sold for £7.5m told he should be playing for Real Madrid by current manager
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal man sold for £7.5m told he should be playing for Real Madrid by current manager

Gennaro Gattuso has told Nuno Tavares that he should be playing for Real Madrid rather than Lazio.

The Italian manager was speaking about his own legacy when he brought up the former Gunners left-back.



3 Tavares joined Lazio on loan in 2024 and made the move permanent the following summer Credit: Getty

Tavares joined Arsenal from Benfica in 2021.

From there, he lasted just one season before joining Marseille on loan, which was followed by a brief spell at Nottingham Forest.

Lazio then signed him in the summer of 2024 on an initial loan before turning that permanent for £7.5million the following summer.

The 26-year-old has established himself with the Italian giants, and Gattuso was very positive in his praise for the Portuguese international.



Speaking to DAZN Italia, he said: "I always said that Tavares is worthy of Real Madrid.

"He feels like someone who lost his parents young, received a big inheritance, and in five years it went up in smoke.



"This is a player who ought to be at Real Madrid. He’s got everything it takes, he has pace, right foot, left foot.

"He is unusual, but after a match he needs his time to recover, but he’s a good lad, you need to get into his head and make him understand.



“He knows he has talent and could’ve had 10/12 years at Real Madrid with his qualities. You’ve just got to get him to understand.”

3 Gattuso is a huge Tavares fan Credit: Getty

Didn't quite work out

Tavares managed 28 appearances for Arsenal in all competitions across the 2021/22 season.

He was mainly at left-back but could operate further forward.

However, he never quite got to grips with the relentless pace of English football and Mikel Arteta was unconvinced.



There was a point near the end of his only season as a first-team player with Arsenal that Kieran Tierney was injured, and Tavares had to step in.

After being substituted in one game, Arteta urged Tavares to respond.

He said: "Throughout your career, you have to go through difficult periods.

"That is the development curve of a player, it is up and down but he is ready and he is willing.

3 Tavares never quite convinced in the Premier League Credit: Getty



"He will be disappointed, but it is part of my job. We have to make decisions to try to win football matches - but it is nothing personal.

"Obviously, I spoke with Nuno because I care a lot about how the players feel, and we are here to make their careers better.

"The decision hurt him. He has to react on that situation because it is a great opportunity to learn a lot in that period in your career."

In the end, he was moved on with various reports suggesting that the Spaniard didn't like his attitude.



But at 26, he now has a stable home and is playing regular football in one of the best leagues in the world.

Sports.title: League Two club announce two games have been postponed in statement
Sports.content:
League Two club announce two games have been postponed in statement

Barnet have announced their fixtures against Crawley Town and York City have been postponed due to international call-ups.

The Bees were initially scheduled to play away at Crawley on September 26 and then host York on October 3.



3 The Bees have been forced to push back two of their league fixtures Credit: Getty

However, because Barnet received confirmation at least three of their players will be away on international duty during the upcoming break, they met the EFL's criteria required to reschedule a game.

What is the EFL's criteria regarding international call-ups?

Per EFL rules, clubs can request a fixture postponement if a player called up for international duty is named in the starting line-up or was a substitute and entered the match before the 75th minute in either 50 per cent of their club's first team matches to date or four of the club's previous five first team games.

Barnet confirmed the club is now in discussions with Crawley, York and other relevant parties to agree new dates and kick-off times.



The Bees' EFL Trophy match away at Wimbledon on October 6 remains unaffected.

How has Barnet performed this season?

Dean Brennan's side have enjoyed an unbeaten start to the 2026/27 League Two campaign, winning three and drawing three of their opening six games.



They remain one of five teams in the fourth tier yet to taste defeat, alongside Walsall, Grimsby Town, Fleetwood Town and Crewe Alexandra.

Key to Barnet's blistering start is their form in front of goal as they have scored a league-leading 14 times.



Leading the Bees' goalscoring charts is Charlie Lakin, who has netted an impressive five times this term.

Two of Lakin's goals came on Saturday in Barnet's 2-1 win over Accrington Stanley.

It was far from a straightforward win for the Bees as they had to come from behind against the Reds, who also went down to 10 men when Devon Matthews was sent off in the second half.

3 The likes of Bees defender Adam Senior have been key in the teams' unbeaten start Credit: Getty



Reacting to the win, Bees boss Brennan hailed his side for a scintillating display that could've done with an extra touch of quality.

However, he voiced his concerns that Barnet had yet again failed to keep their first clean sheet of the campaign.

“I told the players at half-time that was the most dominant performance we had in the first half,” Brennan said.

“We got ourselves into great areas in the final action and phase of play, but needed that extra bit of quality.



“We should have been two or three goals up and I was really shocked with the formation they played.

“We changed our tactics at half-time, played total football and doubled up on the flanks, which paid off with the first goal.

3 Brennan has been in charge of Barnet since September 2021 Credit: Getty

“We limited them to very little chances. Lakin does what he does best in the ‘killer zone’.



“We’re happy with the victory. We need to start getting clean sheets, but winning is everything in football.”

Barnet will look to preserve their unbeaten status when they host Fleetwood on Saturday, with kick-off scheduled for 3pm.

Sports.title: Former Premier League striker goes viral for calling out Howard Webb live on air and hitting out at 'unacceptable' decisions - as ex-ref Dermot Gallagher defends officials after Manchester derby blunder
Sports.content:
Jay Bothroyd has made waves on social media for calling out Pro Ref chief Howard Webb live on Sky Sports.

Webb and his referees have come under fire yet again following their Manchester derby slip up, which saw Erling Haaland's winning goal allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernandez clearly being offside in the build-up.

VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus have been stood down from duty for this weekend as a result of the fallout.

And Bothroyd, who played for the likes of Cardiff and Wolves in his career, has been one of the people leading the backlash as he let loose on Sky.

Bothroyd clashed with former top-level referee Dermot Gallagher, who had claimed referees 'know the law inside out'.

'Why did they get it wrong then?' the former forward asked.

Jay Bothroyd (right) has gone viral after calling out Howard Webb following the Manchester derby officiating blunder

When he was told the officials likely 'lost focus', a frustrated Bothroyd replied: 'This is the thing. To me, that is unacceptable. You can't lose focus. That is their job. Their only job is to look at this - they are under no pressure, they are in a room.

'There is more than one (VAR official). They need to be getting that right, it's as simple as that. And to be saying sorry afterwards, that's not good enough. Let's be real here - Michael Carrick is under pressure now. He could lose his job because of them making a bad decision and saying sorry. "Sorry, Michael, we've made a bad decision, but you've been sacked".'

Sky then showed a clip of Pro Ref chief Howard Webb saying a similar goal that United scored in the derby three years ago 'shouldn't happen again'.

Bothroyd continued: 'First of all, I need to say this, put the camera on me. Howard Webb, come on this show when it's live and speak to us, because you need to explain to us, so I can put you in the spotlight and ask you questions.

'You need to come and speak to me live on this show about this incident. Because I need to know this. We keep on hearing all these things, and I don't understand them.

'There are laws there, and they are not being followed. The understanding. The interpretation. Even yesterday (in the derby), they are saying sorry then trying to explain it and they are digging themselves a bigger hole.

'I don't understand it. I will put my money on it now and say it - this is the easiest decision I'm going to see all year and it's four games in.'

Despite Gallagher's protests, Bothroyd received widespread support for his words.

Erling Haaland's goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernandez standing offside

Fernandez moved to head the ball, clearly impacting United's Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens

One fan wrote on X: 'Jay Bothroyd calling out Howard Webb on live TV was cinema. GOATed behaviour.'

Another posted: 'I watched this live. Jay Bothroyd has never backed down and always real. I love the way he quizzes referee Dermot Gallagher on Ref Watch. He's one of my favourites. Top player. Top analyst. Top man.'

A third shared: 'Standing ovation for Jay Bothroyd. Proper one.'

Webb regularly appears on pre-recorded TNT Sports show 'Match Officials: Mic'd Up', in which he analyses refereeing calls from games.

It was pointed out to Bothroyd that Webb has previously spoken live on incidents, but the forward called for him to go on Sky Sports too.

United defender Lisandro Martinez led the protests from United players after the game.

He said on Sky: 'It's the best league in the world, you have the best teams in the world, the best players in the world, and now we have to go home with this injustice.

'I think it was offside. What I can't understand is the rules. He (Fernandez) was there, in front of me, and I went to him. So that's why Haaland was free at the back.

'It's so hard because you lose a derby and you lose three points at home. Every season they're coming to our club and explaining the rules for an hour-and-a-half. They look so confident, and then after that five or six people are making these kind of mistakes. It's unacceptable.'

Sports.title: Travis Kelce's final season plans: Insiders spill on Taylor marriage pressures, new career decided by couple during 'retirement conversation'... and why he's desperate to avoid same fate as Tom Brady
Sports.content:
When Travis Kelce strolled down the tunnel and into Arrowhead Stadium for the first preseason game of his 14th NFL season last month, the world's attention homed in on one specific aspect of his appearance.

It wasn't his physique. Nor his fitness levels. It wasn't even his signature outlandish fashion sense or his customary preseason 'El Travador' moustache.

No. It was his left ring finger that commanded attention and the glinting gold wedding band now wrapped around it. It was the latest addition to his jewelry collection, a new ring to join the three he has claimed from the Kansas City Chiefs' Super Bowl triumphs.

Yet, when he steps onto the Arrowhead field for the Chiefs' 2026 season opener against the Denver Broncos on Monday night, all talk of star-studded nuptials to the biggest pop star on the planet will fade into the background.

Instead, the question on everyone's lips will be whether he will be walking away from this NFL season with a fifth - and final - ring in his collection.

This offseason has been Kelce's most significant. Six weeks before wandering down Arrowhead's tunnel, the tight end was making his way down the aisle, marrying Taylor Swift in a blockbuster celebration at Madison Square Garden in New York City on July 3.

Chiefs star Travis Kelce is entering his 14th - and perhaps final - season in the NFL

The tight end flashed his gold wedding ring as he entered Arrowhead Stadium in preseason

Kelce, 36, is coming off a milestone offseason having married pop star Taylor Swift in July

Three months earlier, he entered into another contract. The three-time Super Bowl winner announced that NFL retirement would wait, returning for a 14th season.

Yet, while this season may be his first as a married man, it may also be his last ever. If it is, he is making it count.

2025 was a punishing season for Kelce and the Chiefs. Kansas City missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014 - Kelce's second season in the league - their fate sealed by a loss to divisional rivals the Los Angeles Chargers in December, a game which saw Patrick Mahomes fall to an ACL injury.

Kelce, an elder statesman in the Chiefs locker room, was guilty of a number of game-altering errors. He dropped a pass near the goal line in a Week 2 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Another came against the Texans in the game that all but sealed Kansas City's playoff fate.

'Travis is leaning into this year with so much more of an open mind and perspective because the rest of his life is set in stone,' an insider told the Daily Mail.

'Football has been a part of his life forever, but the loss of Patrick last year and his performance on the field really upset him. He didn't want to end things that way.

'Although this season will likely be his last, he wanted to make sure he was in the best shape of his life no matter what.'

The source added: 'All bets are off. He is anticipating it to be the best season ever. That's easier said than done, but that is the goal, and the mentality he is in right now.

Kelce has won three Super Bowls during a remarkable career with the Kansas City Chiefs

But the 2025 season ended in disaster with Kansas City finishing 6-11 and missing the playoffs

'He had his dream wedding, his social life is stuff of legend, he's seen the promised land in his professional life, and he wants to secure at least one more of those moments this year.'

Kelce, it appears, is determined to right his wrongs. If he's going out, he's going out on top. But Kelce may find that harder than expected.

Over the past decade, Kelce has developed a reputation as one of the greatest in his position. Dodging and weaving past opposition defenses, his route-running rivals legendary tight ends.

But now, three weeks shy of turning 37, Kelce is learning that there is no defender harder to shake than Father Time.

Kelce's new wedding ring wasn't the only aspect of his appearance that raised eyebrows during training season. Fans pounced on the veteran, claiming he had finally succumbed to a 'dad bod,' many joking that his new wife was 'feeding him well.'

He was also shrouded in whispered claims from around the league that he is 'done' and his career 'over.'

But when Kelce's career is officially 'over' is a decision only he can make and one that reportedly hinges on the Chiefs' start to the season.

'Several weeks from now, how he is doing, how the team is doing and hopefully being injury free will solidify [his decision on] next year,' our insider said.

Swift and Kelce tied the knot in a star-studded ceremony at Madison Square Garden

Fans mocked Kelce for appearing to have a 'dad bod' during the Chiefs' training camp

'Either way, going into this season as a married man, in the best shape of his life and with Patrick (Mahomes) back, he is like a kid in a candy store.'

Kelce himself has not stated that this will be his last dance. He's also not said anything to the contrary either.

There have, however, been multiple clues fueling the narrative. The most telling came in the form of a photo shared to Instagram by former NFL star and training associate Cris Carter in July.

The image showed Kelce and his long-time trainers. The caption that accompanied it said that the tight end was preparing for 'THE LAST DANCE' alongside 'Next stop Canton/HOF.'

Then, there was the emergence of the $5million new addition to Kelce and Swift's property portfolio. It was revealed this month Kelce has purchased a 131-year-old, recently renovated mansion on the Lake Erie shore near Cleveland, Ohio.

The ultra-private, millionaire enclave perhaps provides a forever home for the A-list couple. Another sign that Kelce is preparing to ride off into the sunset with his new bride, bidding farewell to the NFL once and for all.

For her part, Swift is ready for the happily ever after. Kelce's return to football - beginning with training camp on July 28 - brought a premature end to the couple's honeymoon era.

'Taylor is eager to start a family. As much as one would think that Travis would have to be home for that - and yes, he would - she never wants to pressure him to retire,' the source close to the couple revealed.

The three-time Super Bowl winner purchased a $5million lakefront Ohio mansion in March

Photos obtained by the Daily Mail show inside the sprawling property next to Lake Erie

'Have they talked about him being done? Absolutely. But when he is done, he is still going to be a commentator, do movies and be active. So, if he still wants to play after this year, she would be OK with it. She gets to live her dreams, so he should be able to do the same.

'She would never want him to ever say to her to stop making music and performing, so she is there for him, instead of pressuring him to retire.'

Being forced to spend time apart is nothing uncommon for the newlyweds, whose hectic schedules have provided a challenge ever since they first started dating back in 2023. Swift was on the road with her mammoth world tour while Kelce was hopping from state to state for games.

When he was afforded the time, he joined Swift on the road, jumping onstage for a show in London and even traveling to Buenos Aires, Argentina. They also enjoyed a holiday in Australia.

Swift has spent the past few years juggling work commitments alongside embracing her newfound 'WAG' status. She has been crowned the Queen of Chiefs Kingdom, presiding over the NFL dynasty from her beau's luxury Arrowhead suite with his family and friends. And this season will be no different.

'She will be at all his games, but she will also be busy herself,' the insider shared. 'They have gone through this schedule before, so it is nothing that Taylor is concerned about.

'She's looking forward to enjoying everything this year brings. They are newly married; they are doing everything that they love in their professional life. To enjoy these moments is what it is all about.

'They both know they are very lucky to be in the situation they are in, and they are going to enjoy it all until the wheels fall off. And she loves that they will enjoy it together.'

The Shake It Off hitmaker has supported Kelce at games throughout the past three seasons

Cris Carter has claimed on social media that 2026 will be Kelce's last season in the NFL

Swift is savoring every last moment she can with her NFL beau before the season kicks off. Exclusive photos obtained by the Daily Mail captured the couple emerging from dinner at the Ambassadors Clubhouse in New York on Sunday evening, dressed to the hilt - just over a week before the Chiefs returned to action.

It was one of many pap walks the love birds have taken over the course of their three-year relationship - many of which have fueled accusations of off-field distractions.

Since going public in September 2023, it's been no secret that the pair's high-profile romance has made waves of equal proportion in both Hollywood and the sporting world - with every morsel of their cozy date nights and lavish vacations picked over by music and NFL fans alike.

The couple's jetsetting adventures and lavish nights on the town have coincided with Kelce's dip in form over the two previous seasons. And NFL analysts pointed the finger at Swift.

For a time, it appeared that the grind of more than a decade in the NFL had begun to take its toll. The ritz and razz of his Hollywood lifestyle too tempting. Had Kelce's head been turned by the prospect of celebrity?

Kelce has already dipped his toe into TV and film. He took jobs on the big and small screen - presenting 'Are You Smarter Than a Celebrity,' appearing in 'Grotesquerie' and shooting his cameo in 'Happy Gilmore 2.'

And even he admitted that his focus had wavered as he juggled his relationship with Swift and took his first steps into TV and film.

But now, his dalliances with the silver screen are on pause. For one more season at least, the spotlight is back on the football field.

Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is set to return in Week 1 after an ACL injury last year

Three-time Super Bowl-winner Kelce will turn 37 during the upcoming NFL campaign

Kelce clearly believes he has something left to achieve. A shot at redemption for the Chiefs after a season of misery. He wouldn't have returned if he thought otherwise. The question is: Is it one roll of the dice too many?

Those athletes who go out on top - including NFL greats Peyton Manning and John Elway, who retired after winning the Super Bowl - are far outweighed by heroes who keep coming back for more.

Even Tom Brady is familiar with that fate, performing a retirement U-turn only for his final season to end in sideline tantrums and divorce.

Kelce will be hoping his final chapter follows a different script.

It is perhaps fitting that this season's Super Bowl falls on Valentine's Day. One final win on the NFL's greatest stage would, as Daily Mail's source says, 'be the storybook ending of his career to lead into his forever life with Taylor.'

Sports.title: 'He's got raw power and incredible talent': Meet Aneurin Donald, England's new T20 star - why he won't join in with the football warm-ups, his 'blaze of glory' mantra and how he impressed Brendon McCullum
Sports.content:
It is just over a decade since Aneurin Donald, who will make his England debut in Tuesday's first T20 against Sri Lanka, was terrorising motorists in the usually peaceful north Welsh seaside town of Colwyn Bay. An exaggeration? Only just. Because during the course of a championship innings of 234 off just 136 balls for Glamorgan against Derbyshire in July 2016, aged just 19, he hit 15 sixes, not to mention 26 fours. After making what Wisden described as ‘a sketchy start’, five of his blows dented cars parked in the members’ enclosure, while another assaulted a passing bus. Asked whether he had intended to bring up his 100, 150 and 200 by clearing the ropes, he admitted: ‘Yes, it was in the mind.’ His double-century was, at the time, the joint-fastest in first-class history, equalling Ravi Shastri’s 123-ball blitz for Bombay against Baroda in India’s Ranji Trophy in 1984-85. The only mystery is why it has taken Donald, a former England Under 19s captain, until the age of 29 to play international cricket. Part of the reason is sheer bad luck. Born in Swansea, he left his native Glamorgan towards the end of the 2018 season to join Hampshire, in the hope of boosting his England chances. An incandescent innings of 173 off 144 balls against Warwickshire at Southampton briefly rekindled memories of Colwyn Bay. Aneurin Donald (left) will make his England debut in Tuesday's first T20 against Sri Lanka alongside fellow opener Jos Buttler Donald hit a 19-ball 38 for Trent Rockets in the Hundred final at Lord's, which went down well with England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum But he tore an anterior cruciate ligament playing five-a-side football that winter, ruling him out of the Covid-shortened 2020 season. When he suffered a recurrence of the injury in March 2021, having by his own admission attempted a comeback ‘without a functioning ACL’, he had to miss the whole of that summer too, and described himself as ‘devastated’. Surgery followed, but by the time Donald finally returned to competitive first-team action for Hampshire in May 2022, he had been out of the game for 960 days, missing the prime years of 22 to 25. He averaged just 28 in red-ball cricket that season, and in 2023 didn’t make Hampshire’s Championship team at all, restricted to the Metro Bank One-Day Cup, which by then had become almost a Second XI competition because it clashed with the Hundred, and four games in the T20 Blast which produced 19 runs. But his close shave with retirement had instilled a new determination. When he joined up with the England team this week, he opted against joining in the squad football match, for obvious reasons.

Your browser does not support iframes.

And he decided, as he told Cricinfo recently, to ‘put my best foot forward. I’m going to go down in a blaze of glory. If I’m going to get out, it’s doubling down on what I’m good at.’ Another switch followed, this time to Derbyshire, where his T20 batting has moved to another level. In this year’s competition, his 489 runs at 40 came at the astonishing strike-rate of 230. He also hit more sixes, 37, than anyone in the tournament. In the Hundred, meanwhile, he struck at 217 for Trent Rockets, faster than anyone in the competition with more than 35 runs. His 19-ball 38 in the final came against a Manchester Super Giants attack that included Gus Atkinson, Josh Tongue and Liam Dawson. And while it wasn’t enough to prevent defeat, it went down well with England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum. Two years ago, when McCullum was still Test coach, Donald told Daily Mail Sport: ‘The rhythm of Bazball is something I’ve felt natural for me, since I started playing Championship cricket a little while ago. That’s the gear I play at.’ Donald is hoping to put his interactions with England’s new white-ball batting mentor Kevin Pietersen to good use ‘He’s got a game where he can go from ball one,' says McCullum of his new batting star Now, with injuries to Phil Salt and Jacob Bethell freeing up an opening slot alongside Jos Buttler, Donald – who is hoping to put his interactions with England’s new white-ball batting mentor Kevin Pietersen to good use – will get his chance to show McCullum what England have been missing. ‘He’s a cricketer who has been on our radar for a long time,’ said McCullum, ahead of tomorrow's first T20 at the Utilita Bowl. ‘He’s got a game where he can go from ball one, which is probably quite similar to Salty. 'He’s got raw power. He’s got an incredible amount of talent and I’m looking forward to seeing how he goes on the big stage.’

Sports.title: West Ham legend Ludek Miklosko dead aged 64: Tributes pour in for 'gentle giant' as former Hammers goalkeeper and coach passes away after long battle with cancer
Sports.content:
West Ham legend Ludek Miklosko dead aged 64: Tributes pour in for 'gentle giant' as former Hammers goalkeeper and coach passes away after long battle with cancer

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

West Ham paid tribute to their cult hero and 'gentle giant' Ludek Miklosko who has died at the age of 64.

Miklosko kept 126 clean sheets in eight years with the Hammers and is perhaps best remembered for an inspirational series of saves to deny Manchester United the title in 1995.

The popular Czech, signed from Banik Ostrava for £300,000, later returned to the club as goalkeeper coach and fans have continued to sing his name for many years.

West Ham's players held a moment of silence before training on Monday, and the club will honour him before Wednesday's Carabao Cup third round tie against Fulham.

There are also plans for a tribute at next month's Championship fixture against Queens Park Rangers, where Miklosko spent the final three years of his playing career.

'Rest in peace Ludek, our beloved, inspirational goalkeeper and gentle giant of a man,' said West Ham in a statement released on Monday.

Legendary former West Ham goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko has died aged 64 after a cancer battle

The much-loved Czech 'gentle giant' made 373 outings for West Ham and also played for QPR

'Ludo', left, was a hugely popular figure at West Ham and tributes have been pouring in for him

Miklosko, who won 42 international caps and represent Czechoslovakia at the World Cup in 1990, was diagnosed with cancer in 2021 and announced three years later his decision to withdraw from further treatment.

His son Martin said: 'We are heartbroken to announce the passing of my Dad Ludek, following a brave and courageous battle with cancer.

'On behalf of my Mum and my family, I would like to sincerely thank the fans and everyone at West Ham United Football Club for the kind wishes, thoughts and prayers that were sent to my Dad during his illness.

'We know that the many messages and wishes from his former team-mates and fans alike were a huge sense of comfort to him in his battle with cancer and gave him the strength to not give up and keep fighting for as long as he could.

'We are heartbroken at his loss but take huge comfort from the immense support he received from all of you, along with the knowledge that he is now at peace and no longer suffering.

'Dad simply loved West Ham United, and especially hearing his name sung loud and proud at every game. The club, and its fans, were and always will be a part of our family, so thank you all from the bottom of our hearts.'

Sports.title: Alexander Zverev slammed for 'ultimate disrespect' after calling out Ben Shelton's girlfriend Trinity Rodman in US Open victory speech
Sports.content:
US Open fans have ripped into 'disrespectful' Alexander Zverev after he called out Ben Shelton's girlfriend, Trinity Rodman, during his US Open victory speech.

The 29-year-old finally banished his Flushing Meadows demons, subduing a New York crowd to win 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2 on Sunday afternoon.

Shortly after the match had ended, Zverev jumped on the microphone to deliver his victory speech and made sure to address Shelton's doting partner during it.

On Sunday, Rodman, who played for the NWSL's Washington Spirit earlier in the day, had made a late dash to be in New York for the end of Shelton's US Open final.

'Hey Trinity, I thought you have a game today, no? Well done to you as well. You're the lucky charm, so. Not today, but usually,' Zverev joked.

Rodman appeared to take the address in her stride, laughing along to the German's comments while being shown on the big screen inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Fans have called out Alexander Zverev after he addressed Ben Shelton's girlfriend, Trinity Rodman, during his US Open victory speech after defeating his American rival on Sunday

Soccer star Rodman was left in tears as she watched her boyfriend fall to defeat in the final

"You're the lucky charm … not today but usually.” 😅



Alexander Zverev to Trinity Rodman after he beat her boyfriend Ben Shelton in the US Open Final 🎾 pic.twitter.com/W9q60Yuwor — ESPN (@espn) September 13, 2026

Though neither Rodman nor Shelton took the comments as a slight, fans on social media lamented Zverev for his remarks.

'Bro beat him and took a shot at his girl. Pure humiliation,' one fan wrote on X. 'Alexander Zverev is a menace,' another account added.

'Didnt care much for this mocking of Trin. She has been all class in the support of her BF,' another fan wrote on social media.

One fan wrote: 'Beats him for the title, now trying to steal his gal. Cold,' while another simply called it: 'The ultimate disrespect by Zverev.'

Meanwhile, Shelton has called on tennis bosses to impose a shot clock on second serves in the wake of his US Open final defeat by Zverev – after the No 1 seed routinely bouncing the ball more than a dozen times before hitting his serve.

As it stands, players have 25 seconds to start their first service motion after the end of the previous point. There is no strict time limit on second serves, with the rules stating only that it must be hit 'without delay,' and no maximum number of ball bounces.

Zverev’s habit has sparked calls for change from tennis legends such as Andy Roddick and John McEnroe. And, in the wake of Sunday’s final, Shelton echoed those frustrations.

The German star finally redeemed his heartbreak in Flushing Meadows back in 2020

‘I definitely think for a first serve, you should be able to do whatever you want - you can use the full 25 seconds every time,’ the American said.

‘I think that there should be some sort of rule… limiting time on second serve. You shouldn't have unlimited time. For our sport, for the fans, I think it's tough to be sitting there that long for the next play, the next action to happen.'

Shelton added: ‘I'm sure at some point it will be something that these tournaments look at just because there is such a delay in play in some matches.’

According to reports, Zverev had bounced the ball more than 12,000 times over his first five matches at this US Open. Following his semifinal loss to the German, Karen Khachanov claimed: 'The way he bounces the ball, it annoys not only me, of course, [but] a lot of players.'

Sports.title: Alan Shearer brands Bruno Fernandes 'pathetic' for his role in Phil Foden's red card - and insists referee Michael Oliver was wrong to send off Man City star in Manchester derby
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer brands Bruno Fernandes 'pathetic' for his role in Phil Foden's red card - and insists referee Michael Oliver was wrong to send off Man City star in Manchester derby

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Alan Shearer has hit out at Bruno Fernandes for his role in Phil Foden's red card during the Manchester derby.

Foden received his marching orders in the 23rd minute after he kicked out at the Man United captain, leaving Man City with 10 men for the majority of Sunday's match.

Foden's reaction came after Fernandes appeared to kick him while he was on the ground, before the Portuguese star writhed around in pain.

Despite this, Foden was the only one punished, a decision that Shearer felt was wrong.

'I thought the way Bruno Fernandes went down was pathetic,' he said on The Rest Is Football. 'He helped get Foden off and, yes, he’s kicked out at him a little bit but Bruno Fernandes has also kicked Phil Foden.

'If Phil Foden reacts in the same way as Bruno Fernandes did then both get red cards. So, for me, either both are red or neither of them are.'

Alan Shearer hit out at Bruno Fernandes for his role in Phil Foden's red card on Sunday

Foden kicked out at Fernandes, who had kicked him before writhing around on the floor in pain

Shearer added: 'He’s kicked out, so he’s stupid, OK? But Bruno Fernandes has done the same thing so for me, without doubt, they both should’ve been a red card if Michael Oliver thinks Phil Foden’s is a red card.'

Several other pundits were critical of Fernandes, including Gabby Agbonlahor, who went even further in his assessment of the United skipper.

‘At the end of the day, Bruno Fernandes is a cheat,' he said on talkSPORT. ‘He’s an outstanding player, but he’s a cheat.

‘You’ve kicked Foden twice on the floor, which should have been a red card to you. Then Foden’s lashed out a tiny little bit and you’re rolling around when you’re not hurt.

'A proper referee goes over and says: “You two, cut it out, a yellow each, play on". It’s never a red card.

‘That’s why you get your karma. Maybe the goal that should’ve been disallowed on Haaland, is the karma you sometimes get in football for the red card to Phil Foden.’

The 'karma' Agbonlahor references is in relation to Erling Haaland's winning goal, which was awarded despite Enzo Fernandez appearing to interfere with play while in an offside position.

Although the goal was given following a VAR check, the official refereeing body, Pro Ref, admitted that was the wrong decision and apologised to United later on Sunday evening.

Shearer felt because Foden was sent off, Fernandes should have also been given a red card

In a statement, they said: 'Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

'The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

'In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

'Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.'

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca is proving Pep Guardiola was right to leave Man City, Howard Webb has to go after Man City howler - and the two players who could be in Thomas Tuchel's squad this week: IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca is proving Pep Guardiola was right to leave Man City, Howard Webb has to go after Man City howler - and the two players who could be in Thomas Tuchel's squad this week: IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

If Enzo Maresca is lucky we will one day look back and ask when it was we finally felt he had truly taken hold of Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City and claimed it as his own.

If he is really lucky and if he does enough and wins enough to stick around for the long-term, then we may reflect on derby day in September 2026 as the day we finally drew a line under the years of Guardiola genius.

So far it’s been a slow burn for Maresca at City and that’s because Guardiola still has his name and his principles running right through this City team. Phil Foden, Erling Haaland, Ruben Dias, Rayan Cherki. It’s impossible not to see the great Catalan in so much of what they do.

Equally, it was possible to watch Maresca during Sunday’s win at Manchester United and finally realise and understand that Guardiola was absolutely right to go when he did.

Watch Guardiola on the latest City fly-on-the-wall documentary and you see a man starting to wilt and fray at the edges, a great coach sagging under the weight of ten years of work and expectation and responsibility. A man who by his own admission had very little that was new or fresh to give.

And then you watch Maresca bound down the touch line at full-time – you watch his 10-man team hold Manchester United at bay with cussedness and wit - and suddenly you feel you can see into the future.

Enzo Maresca's appointment has re-energised Manchester City after Pep Guardiola's exit

City were fired up to win the Manchester derby after going down to 10 men in the first half

You see all the energy and vibrancy and freshness that was missing last season. You see a coach nine years younger than his predecessor straining to prove himself to the world just like Guardiola once did.

You see it in his players too. You see it in a player like Elliot Anderson, growing impressively into life at a top club. And you see it in a player like Enzo Fernandez, ready perhaps to show what one can become once you are freed from the circus show that was life at Chelsea.

I was never a fan of Maresca at Stamford Bridge. In fact that is an understatement. I found him an abrasive character whose personality seemed to infect his team. Chelsea were horrible and ugly to watch and, at least in part, I blamed the manager.

But now he, too, is free from that chaos and it shows. Sunday’s derby was a hard watch and ultimately a hard win. But City are four from four in the Premier League and seem ready to stand toe to toe with champions Arsenal.

We have not even reached the first international break yet so we would be wise to tread cautiously. But City look invigorated and rebooted. They look as though they are still learning about Maresca and he about them.

Importantly they look liberated. When Guardiola looked at his players last season he didn’t often see what he hoped to see staring back at him. Typically, he knew it was time to go before we did.

Maresca’s fortune was to be the next one invited through the door. The first thing the Italian appears to have done is bring back a little of the joy. It feels overdue.

REF SHAMBLES IS ON WEBB

Embarrassing. Shambolic. Inept. We have used those words after Manchester derbies before only this time we are not talking about the vanquished team in red.

Manchester United need some work. There is no doubt about that. But they were ultimately beaten by the VAR team on this occasion and how much more of this do we have to take before referees’ chief Howard Webb admits liability and passes the job on to someone else?

Webb – head of the referees’ body in England – is a good guy with sound motives around such subjects as accountability and visibility. He has tried to move things forward.

Howard Webb should be held accountable for VAR's crucial mistake in the Manchester derby

But after a VAR cock-up at Sunderland on Saturday and then the mother of all disasters at Old Trafford, the reputation of our officials continues to disappear down the drain.

Regrettably, Webb has ultimate responsibility for that. His gig, his refs, his show. If they get it right, it’s on him. If they get it wrong, it’s on him.

And right now there is too much wrong, too much catastrophically wrong, for Webb to defend.

Having to write letters to a club like United to apologise for a mistake made in the biggest game of the Premier League weekend reflects abysmally on the body we now call Pro Ref. The name has changed but nothing else has.

It seems that some of Webb’s officials simply don’t know the laws or the game. Or if they do, they don’t know how to apply them.

How can this be? How have we got here? And can we rely on Webb to guide us all back again?

I am not sure we can. It may – sooner or later – be time for a change.

ARTETA CLAIM IS A BIT RICH

It feels ironic that after two years and more of Arsenal getting away with murder at corners and set pieces they finally end up on the wrong end of what is on overdue clampdown on grappling and wrestling.

How the VAR officials didn’t realise that Ezri Konsa was pulled to the ground by Sunderland defender Dan Ballard after referee John Brooks had called it the other way round seemed set to sit as the worst oversight of the weekend before events at Old Trafford stole their thunder a day later.

Mikel Arteta's claim that referees need to 'protect the game' landed rather hypocritically

Certainly Sunderland shouldn’t have been awarded their spot-kick – ultimately saved by David Raya – but for Arteta to subsequently talk about an obligation on referees to ‘protect the game’ was a bit rich.

His players, after all, have been pushing right at the edges of what is legal at set pieces for so long it has become an indelible part of the champions’ identity.

Arteta spoke of his love for the ‘beautiful game’ this week. At times he has appeared to take liberties with the meaning of the word.

BIN THE USELESS CHAT

I have listened to Marc Guehi talk enough times on England duty to know the City defender is not prone to giving much away. Some footballers are like that and it’s entirely their prerogative. They are paid to play, not talk.

Suffice to say, then, that when I saw Patrick Davison attempting to glean some insight from Guehi at half-time on Sky that I rather knew how it was going to end.

Davison did his best. As indeed he did when moving on to what we could generously call a chat with United manager Michael Carrick as he exited the tunnel for the start of the second half.

But what did we learn? Nothing, of course. What was said of interest? Nothing, of course.

These interval exchanges of utter nothingness are now part of the TV rights holders’ package of entitlement for this season and are an utter waste of time.

Footballers and managers are asked to do more and more media these days as SKY, TNT and the rest seek full return on the millions of pounds they invest in the Premier League this season.

But this is a step too far. Nobody wants or needs it. Play some white noise if you have too. It would be cheaper and in all likelihood more interesting.

QUIZ TIME

Question: Which former star of both Manchester clubs remains so in love with United that he was seen and heard belting out ‘Take me Home, United road.’ in the Old Trafford press box before kick-off yesterday? He was also getting rather angry as the game slipped away from United.

*Answer at foot of the page.

WILL THE REAL MARTINEZ PLEASE STAND UP?

Raya’s performance at the Stadium of Light only strengthened my view expressed last week that he is now the best goalkeeper in the Premier League.

At Chelsea, meanwhile, they are still waiting to see what version of Emi Martinez has turned up at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea’s capture of Martinez for £7.5m is understandably viewed as a steal in these days of sky high transfer fees. It may well turn out to be so. But that overlooks the fact that he was rarely at his brilliant best for Villa last season.

Martinez, 34, was fabulous for Argentina in the World Cup final but he was erratic in the draw against Hull on Saturday. Chelsea have long since needed some calm in goal. We wait to see if this one actually works out.

SOLANKE KEY TO SPURS CHANCES

There was actually some better attacking football from Tottenham - particularly in the first half - in their draw against Everton but the fact Roberto de Zerbi's team still haven't scored a Premier League goal is starting to have a pub quiz ring to it.

Omar Marmoush - recently signed from Manchester City - always carries a threat but it feels as though he is more productive playing behind a centre forward than he is when asked to lead the line on his own.

The question is whether Dominic Solanke is really good enough to take Spurs where they wish to go as that central striker.

The 28-year-old cost £55m two summers ago but only has 12 league goals to his name.

It’s fair to say, he has something to prove.

Dominic Solanke has to prove his worth in attack amid Tottenham's worrying goal drought

GRAVITY WILL TAKE ITS TOLL ON BRAVE EVERTON

Tottenham do at least have a strong bench these days. Against Everton, De Zerbi’s options as substitutes included James Maddison, Mohammed Kudus, Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher. It feels as though progress must come.

But Everton – unbeaten so far – are not so blessed which rather makes a mockery of Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall’s assertion that David Moyes’ team can challenge for Europe this season.

Dewsbury-Hall is an intelligent footballer and has bought in to Moyes’ team-orientated philosophy on Merseyside. But it’s impossible to escape the fact that a dreadful transfer window has left Everton open to the forces of gravity.

Everton sit eighth in the Premier League and all credit to them for draws against Spurs, Manchester United and Bournemouth and a win over Crystal Palace. It’s been an incredible early season effort.

But logic tells us it simply can’t last and it won’t.

COVENTRY BLUES BAD NEWS FOR THE FA

Frank Lampard’s problems at Coventry – last season’s Championship winners are also yet to score a goal – may yet prove to be an issue for the FA.

The Coventry manager has long since been identified as a potential England manager by the national governing body.

But that’s going to be a hard sell to the public if the 48-year-old doesn’t make a go of it in the top-flight with Coventry.

It’s early days for the Sky Blues on their return to the Premier League and common sense would suggest Lampard gets a long stretch to make things right. It was notable yesterday that after a thumping 5-0 home defeat to Brighton, he was still getting backed to the hilt by the home fans.

But since when did common sense and fan opinion have a home in the football world?

Lampard, of course, has already had two middling spells in the top division, at Chelsea and Everton. He really needs to get this one right.

Coventry's poor start to the season under Frank Lampard continued with a 5-0 loss to Brighton

TUCHEL EYES KING AND SCOTT

Current England manager Thomas Tuchel has a big date in his diary for this Friday when he names his first squad since the World Cup.

With that Atlanta surrender against Argentina still fresh in everybody’s mind, Tuchel will be under pressure to make some changes for the four Nations League games against Spain, Croatia and Czechia (twice) that make up a mammoth three-week international break later this month.

Tuchel took 26 players to America whereas this will be a 23-man party.

So three names will have to go at least and it feels as though there will be significantly more casualties with Cole Palmer and Phil Foden pushing for returns and good early season form from Bournemouth’s Alex Scott and Fulham’s Josh King – watched in person by Tuchel nine days ago – places them at the front of the queue for what feels like an inevitable midfield reshuffle.

EMERY RISK UNDERMINES VILLA

Aston Villa’s decision to place the Europa League trophy in the players’ tunnel ahead of their game with Nottingham Forest was certainly ballsy given that it was their midlands rivals they beat in the semi-final en route to last season’s triumph in Istanbul.

If the Forest players were fired up by having to walk past a trophy they came close to winning then they used it to their advantage in a one-sided game that featured a welcome return to form for striker Liam Delap. His opening goal – rifled in from 25 yards – was his first in 28 games.

Using all five substitutes before Ian Maatsen's injury was a risk from Aston Villa's Unai Emery

Villa are doing it tough with one point and one goal from four Premier League games and weren’t helped by their manager Unai Emery on Saturday.

Emery had used all five subs by the time Ian Maatsen left the field injured late in the piece. In fact Emery had used them all by the 63rd minute and whichever way you look at it, that’s a risk.

*QUIZ ANSWER: Peter Schmeichel.

Sports.title: John McEnroe's 'unprofessional' and 'belittling' comments are slammed as the 'final straw' by angry US Open fans
Sports.content:
ESPN is facing calls to axe John McEnroe after he controversially pleaded for Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz to return to their best in wake of Alexander Zverev's US Open win.

Zverev sealed a second Grand Slam of the year with a four-set victory over home favorite Ben Shelton on Sunday.

The No 1 seed, whose service routine has sparked calls for a rule change, broke the hearts of a New York crowd who hoped Shelton would become the first American man to win a major since 2003.

But he was beaten 6-3 7-6 5-7 6-2 by Zverev and afterwards a clip went viral from ESPN's coverage of the US Open final.

'So the drought continues but the rebirth of Sascha Zverev also continues into 2027 - Down Under awaits, huh?' lead announcer Chris Fowler said, looking ahead to the Australian Open.

'Get healthy Carlos and Jannik!' responded McEnroe, the seven-time Grand Slam singles champion who serves as an analyst alongside his brother Patrick.

This is how the commentary feed ended after the Zverev and Shelton US Open trophy ceremony.



"Get healthy Carlos and Jannik."



"Please"



😭😭😭😭😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/sUbWxJXQAa — The Tennis Letter (@TheTennisLetter) September 13, 2026

John McEnroe is facing a backlash over his comments after Alexander Zverev's US Open win

Zverev sealed a second Grand Slam of the year with a four-set victory over Ben Shelton

Both Alcaraz and Sinner have battled injury issues over recent months, with world No 1 Sinner missing the US Open with a knee problem, while Alcaraz returned at Flushing Meadows after more than four months out with wrist damage.

But McEnroe's comments sparked fury among some fans, who accused the tennis legend of being 'unprofessional' and 'belittling the sport.'

'Sorry, this should be the final straw for John McEnroe,' one supporter wrote. 'Unprofessional, belittling the sport and stealing the spotlight from the champion and runner up seconds after victory.'

Another added: 'McEnroe has to go. Carlos is healthy and he played, It's not Zverev's fault that Jannik's knee doesn't work. It's his moment and he won fair and square… this is honestly pathetic.'

Others defended the 67-year-old, however, insisting his comments were part of a discussion looking forward to the 2027 season. 'It’s exactly what most tennis fans are thinking,' one said.

It is not the first time that McEnroe has faced a backlash over comments he made at this US Open. He was earlier accused of being 'disrespectful' in the wake of Novak Djokovic's first-round exit.

After Djokovic was beaten by world No 49 Mariano Navone, McEnroe joked that the Argentine would be 'playing [his] second round on Court 21.'

Sports.title: Man Utd VAR stood down after Erling Haaland incident as Howard Webb takes action
Sports.content:
Man Utd VAR stood down after Erling Haaland incident as Howard Webb takes action

The video assistant referees at the centre of the Erling Haaland Manchester United vs Man City controversy in the Premier League have been stood down by Pro Ref

View 2 Images Erling Haaland's goal against Manchester United was controversially allowed to stand after a lengthy VAR check (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus have been stood down from officiating duty in the wake of the Manchester derby controversy. Donohue and Antrobus were in the video assistant referee booth for Sunday's 1-0 win for Manchester City over rivals United after Erling Haaland's second-half winner.

‌



Chief Refereeing Officer Howard Webb and the management team are said to have made the decision, which will see the pair out of action at least until after the international break. It comes after Haaland's effort was given despite the on-field decision initially being offside.

‌



It was claimed at the time that the Norwegian was in an onside position with Patrick Dorgu's outstretched leg playing him on and Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, hadn't interfered with play despite making an attempt to connect with Josko Gvardiol's cross.

‌



Robin van Persie lands new job as ex-Man Utd ace recovers from shock managerial exit READ MORE :

OPINION Erling Haaland and Man City are now on a mission to prove a point about Pep Guardiola by Andy Dunn

Lisandro Martinez was caught between the offside Fernandez and Haaland, who was behind him. The Argentine was left incensed by the decision and was forced to hold back during an angry interview with Sky Sports on Sunday.

Michael Carrick was also left exasperated from the incident and admitted he was left 'very worried' by the perception from the officials. Pro Ref, formerly the PGMOL, later apologised for an 'error of judgement'.

‌



A Pro Ref spokesperson said: "Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland - that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

‌



"In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

View 2 Images Haaland's goal was eventually given after a long VAR check (Image: Getty Images)

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

Article continues below

Donohue was the lead video assistant referee for the Manchester derby and has not been appointed a top-flight fixture this weekend, a first this term after being involved in three Premier League matches so far. He will not be on duty for the Carabao Cup third round either which sees European clubs in cup action.

The organisation were forced to U-turn on the suggestion that the former Chelsea man hadn't interfered with play following an Premier League Match Centre tweet on X.

It read: "VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball."

Sports.title: Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning EuroMillions when epic charity runs get tough
Sports.content:
Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning EuroMillions when epic charity runs get tough

Sir Kevin Sinfield, who has raised £11million from his previous six fundraising events, describes his latest effort - seven ultramarathons in seven days - as "doing a bit of running for a mate" in Rob Burrow

Kevin Sinfield on his last MND challenge

Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning the EuroMillions when the going gets tough in his epic MND charity runs.

‌



The shy superhero has raised £11million from his previous six fundraising events. He describes his latest effort - seven ultramarathons in seven days - as "doing a bit of running for a mate". The friend is rugby league legend and Sir Kevin's former team mate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024 after living with motor neurone disease (MND) for more than four years.

‌



Dad-of-two Sir Kevin dreams of winning the lottery to fund a cure for the disease - and buy a new car for his dad Ray - in times of need. Asked how he handles the mental battle of running more than 30 miles a day, he said: "I dream of winning the EuroMillions. That is my favourite one.

‌



"It is always the same amount, my dad always gets a new car. Then we cure MND with it."

Rugby legend Kevin Sinfield finally knighted in Birthday Honours for MND fundraising heroics READ MORE :

View 5 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning the lottery on his epic runs (Image: Danny Lawson/PA Wire)

Sir Kevin Sinfield launches latest MND fundraiser

Speaking at Old Trafford where he launched his last fundraiser at the SuperLeague Dream Team event, he admitted that the training "just gets harder" as you grow older.

‌



His aim is to help as many MND sufferers as possible. Rob Burrow, his former Leeds Rhinos team mate, raised more than £20m for MND research. Sir Kevin has added another £11m.

Sir Kevin told how his latest venture will help research to find a cure, and support those who have been diagnosed with the disease.

"I finished the last block of running on Saturday which was my birthday. The challenge now is to stay fit and healthy and be really smart for the next two weeks," he said.

‌



View 5 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield carries his best friend Rob Burrow over the finishing line of the Leeds Marathon in 2023 (Image: Danny Lawson/PA Wire)

"I have not trained harder; it just gets harder and I am getting older. It would be great to find a cure, we are still a fair stretch from that. The cure is the dream for everyone involved.

"In the short term, we have to help the families diagnosed today and tomorrow. We are letting them down, and that has been the case for decades. We can help them.

‌



"Then there is the awareness because it makes such a difference when people know and understand this condition.

"Over past three and four years, at the stops in the running, we have brought people together, and that shows the love support for the MND families.

"And can share in grief for the families who have lost loved ones. I am a shy bloke; I have love for the team who have been immense through all this."

‌



View 5 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield is now an England rugby union coach (Image: Danny Lawson/PA Wire)

'We did this for Rob'

Asked about the secret of his success, he said they had been "incredibly lucky" with the timing of their first effort during Covid.

He added: "There were no other charity or sporting events, and people wanted to give their money, it was just incredible. I never forget why we started this - it was to run for Rob, it has always been about doing a bit of running for a mate.

‌



"I did a half marathon on Saturday and then had a recovery, and I went for a meal as most people do for their birthday. Juggling family time and work is tough for everybody preparing for a marathon. It is just the same for me."

He has just returned from South Africa where he said he was "chased by a pack of dogs" while training. He has also been to Argentina, where he was told that he might have to 'barricade himself in the hotel' in Buenos Aires during the England v Argentina World Cup semi final.

He has completed an incredible 500km of training over the past few weeks. The dad, from Oldham, Greater Manchester, has also been in touch with Jai Arrow, the forward for the South Sydney Rabbitohs, who announced his immediate retirement from the National Rugby League (NRL) in May after being diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) at age 30.

‌



View 5 Images Sir Kevin on his Ultra 7 challenge in 2022 (Image: PA)

'There is a war to be won against MND'

Sir Kevin is Australia next year for the rugby World Cup and 'has an idea' about doing one more charity event abroad. But he wanted to bring the curtain down on his UK exploits, with a tour of the rugby league grounds of the North at the end of this month.

"I needed to release the team, and this is something I could do," he added. "The support for Rob and the Burrow family in Leeds is always great.

‌



"I look forward to going back there thanks to my history with the city. I'm also really looking forward going back to the North West, seeing the people who have supported us.

"I know it will be an incredible week. It sounds strange given the rivalry but I always get a warm welcome in Hull and I love going there.

"All the Superleague clubs have been great, after the final on October 3 is over, and the battle is over, there is a war to be won against MND and I hope they can help with that."

‌



He admits that he still "does not like running" but added: "I makes you a better person, and a bit kinder. I would always encourage people to exercise, getting out there in the open air is so good for you, for your mental health. The good thing is that people are always nice to me now.

"Opposition clubs were always respectful to me after I retired from the game, and we have seen the best of our home nations. The fans always turn up with a big smile which is so important and the nice thing is that people don't just talk bout rugby now, they talk about running and the MND community."

View 5 Images Sir Kevin and Rob Burrow are pictured at an event in May 2023 (Image: PA)

‌



Sir Kevin, who turned 46 on Saturday, will visit all 12 English Betfred Super League grounds from Sept 27 to Oct 3 as he completes seven ultra marathons in seven days.

Now an England rugby union coach, he has already completed six epic endurance challenges for MND research. He will start at Hull Kingston Rovers on September 28 and call in at the grounds of the 11 other English top-flight rugby league clubs along the way.

The "7 in 7: The Grand Finale" venture is set to finish on the pitch at Old Trafford ahead of the Super League Grand Final. As part of his challenge, he will run a mile each day alongside people affected by the neurodegenerative illness.

Article continues below

Each day will be separated into 7 km blocks, which Sinfield has to complete within an hour. His route will take him across the Pennines on day five, and that day he will visit Wigan Warriors and Leigh Leopards.

The last run sets off at St Helens, calls at Warrington Wolves, and then heads to Manchester. You can find out full details of this year’s challenge using this link.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland and Man City are now on a mission to prove a point about Pep Guardiola
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland and Man City are now on a mission to prove a point about Pep Guardiola

The world's best manager left at the end of last season after ten glorious and successful years but Enzo Maresca has got his Manchester City side refreshed and raring to go

View 3 Images Erling Haaland could not stop smiling after Manchester City's win at Old Trafford (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Arne Slot’s version of Liverpool in the early stages of the 2025-26 season is a warning to any Premier League manager. Five Premier League matches, five wins, including a victory in the Merseyside derby.

‌



And Slot already had a title in the bank. So when it comes to reading significance into a small sample of games in August and September, the reservations are obvious.

‌



But watching Manchester City on and off the pitch at Old Trafford, it was hard not to wonder if this is a squad that has been re-energised by the managerial change. That sounds heinous to suggest, obviously.

‌



And don’t forget, Pep Guardiola did bow out by winning two trophies in his final season and his team finished as Premier League runners-up. Hardly a shabby campaign.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



But even though Guardiola also counted a Manchester derby win - a less controversial 3-0 verdict at the Etihad - amongst his early successes last season, his side lost two of their opening four Premier League games. Enzo Maresca has won four out of four, complementing those wins with a 2-0 Champions League victory in Porto.

All four Premier League wins have been in different styles but the players have quickly bought into Maresca, it seems. Not just the players.

Everyone is happy if your club has just won a Manchester derby with ten men on opposition turf. That goes without saying.

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Maresca has had the perfect start as Manchester City manager (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

But the reaction of the backroom staff - of which there were plenty - was as involved and as euphoric as City supporters have probably seen for quite some time. Again, it is understandable when you win by a single goal at Old Trafford, having had a player very harshly dismissed early doors.

But it was still significant. If some players and staff have been refreshed by a change of voice and approach, it would not be the biggest surprise. Guardiola was a very demanding manager. Brilliant but demanding, a perfectionist.

‌



Maresca could well turn out to be similarly demanding, but he is still getting to know the different characters at the club. The jury will be out for some time on Maresca’s chances of making a decent fist of the impossible job of following a decade of Pep’s brilliance. Of course it will. He will be measured in trophies.

But derby wins for City do not come much more treasured than the one he helped produce at Old Trafford. Tactically, he got it spot-on, his deployment of Iliman Ndiaye a mini masterstroke. And it is clear he likes a gritty player. Who doesn’t?

View 3 Images Pep Guardiola delivered hundreds of half-time speeches to his Manchester City players (Image: Prime Video)

‌



Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez were arch-disruptors against United and you can expect Maresca’s City to be perhaps a little more feisty than they were under Guardiola. And you can expect them to rise to the challenge.

Guardiola is and was a genius. But Erling Haaland and the players he has left at the Etihad - and, true, a few have gone - will be out to prove a point.

It might only be subconsciously, but they will be out to prove that City’s success over the past ten years was not just down to one man. And perhaps that is why the celebrations at the end of the derby win were even more euphoric.

Sports.title: Robin van Persie lands new job as ex-Man Utd ace recovers from shock managerial exit
Sports.content:
Robin van Persie lands new job as ex-Man Utd ace recovers from shock managerial exit

Ex-Manchester United and Arsenal ace Robin van Persie is now embarking on a new project after his first senior managerial role came to an end

View 3 Images Robin van Persie has recently started a new role (Image: 2026 BSR Agency)

Former Manchester United and Arsenal forward Robin van Persie has become a global ambassador for e-bike brand ENGWE. At the end of last season, Van Persie's managerial role with Feyenoord came to an end after 16 months.

He earned Champions League qualification with the Dutch side after finishing second in the Eredivisie but was surprisingly relieved of his duties. The ex-striker's exit took place not long after the club appointed Devy Rigaux as technical director and Robert Eenhoorn as general manager.

Now, a few months after his departure, it's been announced that the Dutchman, who scored 144 goals and contributed 59 assists in 280 Premier League appearances, will work in an ambassadorial capacity for the global e-bike brand.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

After the new role with ENGWE was announced, Van Persie said: "Throughout my career, reliability has always mattered. Being able to trust the people around you, your equipment and your decisions.

"That is one of the things that attracted me to ENGWE. Today, staying active and finding better ways to move are just as important to me.”

A spokesperson for the brand also said: " Robin represents performance, discipline and reliability, but also an active way of life that goes far beyond football.

View 3 Images Robin van Persie has become the company's latest ambassador (Image: ENGWE)

"Together, we want to make e-mobility a more natural part of everyday life and inspire more people to move, explore and enjoy every ride.”

Van Persie is yet to return to football after leaving Feyenoord, who hired his former Netherlands team-mate and ex-Rangers manager Giovanni van Bronckhorst as his successor.

He still has a firm connection to the club, with his son Shaqueel van Persie turning out for the Dutch giants. Last season, the ex-United forward was the one who gave Shaqueel his senior debut for the Rotterdam side.

View 3 Images Van Persie is yet to return to football (Image: 2026 Koji Watanabe)

When asked why he turned to his son, who is also a left-footed striker, during a 3-1 Europa League defeat to Celtic, Van Persie replied: "I made that call as a coach, not as a dad because we needed a goal.

"Shaqueel is a player who can score a goal from all angles. That was the reason I brought him on. From a father's point of view, when your son makes his debut that is always a special moment. But I wasn't that busy with enjoying that moment, I was doing my work like Shaqueel was."

Sports.title: Top jockey flies from Australia to audition for chance to beat Luke Littler for £501k
Sports.content:
Top jockey flies from Australia to audition for chance to beat Luke Littler for £501k

Zac Spain, who calls himself ‘The Darting Jockey’, will try out for one of 20 places up for grabs in the new Netflix show ‘Beat Luke Littler’

View 3 Images Zac Spain: auditioning for role in new Luke Littler darts show

A top jockey is flying 10,000 miles from Australia to audition for the chance to take on Luke Littler for a £501,000 prize.

‌



Melbourne-based Zac Spain, 30, has ridden nearly 700 winners including two at Group 1 level. But while regularly hitting the board on the track, he also hits 180s off it as a darts player, ranked 15 in Australia by the World Darts Federation.

‌



On Sunday Spain rode his fifth winner of the campaign at Sale, Victoria, the day before he was set to catch a flight to Britain. He has accepted an invitation to try out for one of 20 places up for grabs for the new Netflix show ‘Beat Luke Littler’.

‌



The programme offers part-time players a chance to take on world number one Littler in a single leg and earn £501,000 if they can beat him.

The two-time Professional Darts Corporation world champion Littler says: “Everyone thinks they can beat me. Now they get a chance to prove it.”

View 3 Images Luke Littler will front a new Netflix show in which everyday darts players will go up against the world number one for a chance to win £501,000. (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



Spain has accepted an invitation to an in-person audition for the October 30 live show for which former Match of the Day host Gary Lineker and TV presenter and author Richard Osman have been signed up.

Spain, who calls himself ‘The Darting Jockey’, told followers of his Instagram, “A lot of people have been selected to try out for the auditions for ‘Beat Luke Littler’ the Netflix show which is going to be coming out.

View 3 Images Zac Spain: calls himself 'The Darting Jockey'

‌



“You get selected for a one leg 501 to try to beat him to win £500,000. I am going to give it a crack and fly to Manchester because that’s where it is.

“If I get it, I get it. If I don’t, I don’t. I think it’s just something I signed up for not thinking I would get selected.

“I’ve booked flights. I leave on the 14th and I’m back on the 22nd. I am going to vlog the journey. What’s the worst that can happen? I don’t get selected and I come back home.”

Article continues below

He added: “It’s going to be tough but if I can get through the first stage and get to speak to producers I think I’ve got a pretty good story behind me.”

Sports.title: John McEnroe slammed for 'unprofessional' comments immediately after US Open final
Sports.content:
John McEnroe slammed for 'unprofessional' comments immediately after US Open final

Alexander Zverev won the US Open on Sunday, but John McEnroe's comments about Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner after the final have sparked backlash

View 2 Images John McEnroe has been slammed for his comment following the US Open final. (Image: Joe Buglewicz, Getty Images)

Tennis legend John McEnroe has been criticised for his comment when signing off his commentary of the US Open final. Alexander Zverev beat home favourite Ben Shelton in the final at Flushing Meadows to claim his second Grand Slam title of the year.

‌



Zverev came out as 6-3, 7-6, 5-7, 6-2 winner over Shelton. The win backs up the French Open title he claimed back in the summer, topping off a memorable year for the German.

‌



One thing that has been levelled at Zverev is the absence of both Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner from the tournaments. The former missed the French Open, while the latter missed the US Open, with both knocked out in the early rounds of the other Grand Slam.

‌



Aryna Sabalenka loses it with cameraman immediately after US Open final loss in TV outburst READ MORE :

US Open champ Aryna Sabalenka angrily hits back at reporter during press conference READ MORE :

Zverev won't be bothered, given that the record books will show him as the dominant presence across the majors in 2026. But McEnroe clearly is, given the American tennis icon concluded his commentary work with ESPN by stating: "Get well soon, Carlos and Jannik," reports the Express.

The six-word remark could be viewed as an innocent goodwill message, but there are suggestions there was more spite behind it. So much so, McEnroe has attracted considerable backlash, with some claiming it is disrespectful to Zverev.

View 2 Images Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton in the US Open final. (Image: Matthew Stockman, Getty Images)

‌



One fan posted on X: "You may like or dislike Alexander Zverev, but it wasn't the best moment to make that comment" Another added: "McEnroe a sore US loser right there! Arrogant as Shelly!"

Another tennis fan said claimed: "Unbelievably disrespectful." One called for a tougher stance from ESPN and wrote: "Unfortunately, neither of us McEnroe brothers have been known for their tactful commentary. @espn needs to let them go. There's plenty retired tennis players who could do a much better job."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



However not everyone disagreed, some even welcomed the change, saying: "I was so relieved we didn't have another Sincaraz final, quite frankly. Was getting so bored of it!

"And so many of the other men are fun to watch. So I enjoyed this final!"

They were among the minority on social media as another said: "Sorry, this should be the final straw for John McEnroe. Unprofessional, belittling the sport and stealing the spotlight from the champion and runner-up seconds after victory."

Article continues below

The match to came to an end in a strange manner with Zverev unaware that he had won the title. After Shelton's forehand return hit the net at match point to Zverev, the German calmly turned and walked towards the service line.

ESPN commentator Chris Fowler. "At long last, Alexander Zverev is a US Open champion."

McEnroe then added: "I don't think he knows it's over."

Sports.title: Team GB golden girl Amy Hunt hits back at Sydney Sweeney as Hollywood star faces backlash
Sports.content:
Team GB golden girl Amy Hunt hits back at Sydney Sweeney as Hollywood star faces backlash

Team GB sprinter Amy Hunt hit out at American actress Sydney Sweeney during a post-race interview at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship

View 2 Images Sprinting sensation Amy Hunt has criticised actress Sydney Sweeney (Image: BBC)

Team GB's Amy Hunt has joined the growing list of elite athletes criticising actress Sydney Sweeney over a controversial sports gambling ad campaign. Hunt took aim at the Hollywood star following her performance at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest.

‌



This year has been a breakout one for British sprinter Hunt. She claimed a record-breaking four gold medals at the European Championships earlier this summer to go with her 4 x 100m relay silver medal won at Paris 2024.

‌



On Saturday and Sunday, Hunt competed at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in tough 100m and 200m fields. The competition does not hand out traditional medals or have a podium, and each event winner receives a specially designed trophy. Hunt finished eighth in the 100m in 11.09s as Melissa Jefferson-Wooden emerged victorious.

‌



The 24-year-old then clocked a season's best 22.10s in the 200m after making the final but could only manage fourth. America's Jefferson-Wooden also won this event in 21.47s, the fourth fastest women's 200m time in history.

‌

"Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like," Hunt exclaimed. Referencing Jefferson-Wooden's winning time, she said: "21.4. Muscles. Hard work, blood, sweat, tears. This is a beautiful evening."

US-based sports prediction market app Novig released a campaign starring Sweeney earlier this month. The actress, who is an equity partner and investor in the company, appears in a series of ads.

‌



In these, Sweeney is either completely nude or wearing minimal clothing, often using various sporting equipment to cover herself and mock-playing sports. They were primarily distributed on platforms such as YouTube, TikTok and Instagram.

Several athletes have condemned the campaign, including American gymnast Gracie Kramer, who captioned one of her training montages: "I don't know what Sydney Sweeney was doing, but this is what women in sport look like."
