World.title: French Judiciary Prepares Warrant for Suspected Jean-Michel Nicolier Murderer
World.content:
September the 13th, 2026 – The French judiciary is currently preparing an international arrest warrant for Spasoje Petković, known as “Štuka”, the suspected Jean-Michel Nicolier murderer.

The French judiciary is preparing an international arrest warrant for Spasoje Petković, known as Štuka, suspected of the murder of French volunteer Jean-Michel Nicolier at Ovčara back in 1991. Index reports that news of progress in the investigation being conducted in Paris has brought new hope to the Nicolier family that justice will finally be served after 35 years. The family’s lawyer confirmed that the investigating judge at the War Crimes Department of the court in Paris is currently working on the warrant. Paul Nicolier, brother of the murdered Vukovar defender, told RTL that they received the news with “great satisfaction and deep emotion.”

the nicolier family will never give up on justice

“We’re extremely grateful to the French judicial authorities for all their efforts. We hope that, 35 years after the murder, all the circumstances of his death will finally be clarified and that those responsible for it will answer before the court,” said Paul Nicolier. He emphasised that this is an extremely important step that the family has been waiting for years and that sends a clear message: “Thirty-five years after the crime, the judiciary has not given up, and neither have we.” He stressed that the family has always wanted only the truth and justice for Jean-Michel. “Our lawyers Ghislain Dubois and Arnaud Bilen have our full and unconditional trust. We sincerely thank them for their commitment, determination and tireless work. For Jean-Michel, for our family and for his memory, we will go all the way,” concluded the brother of the murdered volunteer.

previous demands to serbia to extradite the suspected murderer fell on deaf ears

The Nicolier family had previously threatened Serbia with a private lawsuit and, through the embassy in Paris, demanded the urgent extradition of Štuka. According to information published by RTL, France has already questioned Petković, and the investigation is nearing its end. He told the French judge that he is not guilty, but investigators have reportedly gathered sufficient evidence against him. During the investigation, several people were questioned in Croatia and Serbia. One of the last persons questioned was someone hiding in Norway, who is suspected of having participated in the relocation of mass graves at Ovčara.

The exact location of Spasoje Petković Štuka is not known. It is only known that he lives under a changed identity at a secret location. Jean-Michel Nicolier joined the defence of Croatia in the summer of 1991 as a member of HOS. After being wounded in Vukovar, he was transferred to the hospital, where he awaited the fall of the city. From there, members of the JNA and Serbian paramilitary units took him to Ovčara. According to the testimonies of survivors, he was tortured and killed at Ovčara. His remains were only exhumed after 34 years from a mass grave. In the court proceedings for the crimes at Ovčara conducted in Belgrade, Štuka had the status of a repentant witness. He allegedly admitted guilt in exchange for freedom, and several witnesses accused him of the murder. One of them stated that Štuka, after killing Nicolier, even went as low as to steal 20 francs from his pocket.

World.title: Rijeka Gateway Establishes Cooperation With Huge Shipping Companies
World.content:
September the 13th, 2026 – In its first year of commercial operation, Rijeka Gateway has successfully established cooperation with the two largest shipping companies in the world, Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd.

Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that the terminal has received more than a thousand trains and over 80 thousand trucks since opening, and the current ratio of cargo transport from the terminal is 42 percent by rail and 58 percent by road. Rijeka Gateway is the technologically most advanced container terminal in this part of Europe, in the first year since the start of commercial operations has created a team of 422 employees, raised the terminal to a high level of operational excellence required by the global APM Terminals network, received over 100 ships and handled more than 370 thousand TEU of cargo.

Additionally, the terminal has strengthened Rijeka’s logistical position between large Asian ports and the Mediterranean within the Gemini shipping network, and new logistical routes have been opened so that Rijeka is connected by regular rail links with Serbia, Hungary and Austria, as well as with important ports on the Adriatic and in Italy, it was highlighted at a press conference organised on the occasion of the first anniversary of commercial operations of Rijeka Gateway.

In the first year of commercial operations, Rijeka Gateway successfully established cooperation with the two largest shipping companies in the world, Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd, both of which use this terminal as their transhipment hub for import and export cargo from Italy. Rijeka Gateway has additionally confirmed its role as a regional logistical hub for container traffic within the Adriatic and is currently the only terminal on the Adriatic that performs this type of operations within the Gemini network. Information indicates that the lowland railway project has finally received the long-desired “acceleration”, which is necessary due to the new phase of development of the Rijeka terminal.

the gemini network

Rijeka Gateway has also confirmed its role as a regional logistical hub for container traffic within the Adriatic and is currently the only terminal on the Adriatic that performs this type of operations within the Gemini network – an operational cooperation between the companies Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd, which covers seven main global trade routes and serves to accelerate and optimise traffic, and Rijeka Gateway is a key port of call within the Gemini cooperation on the line connecting large Asian ports with the Mediterranean. Thus Rijeka is additionally connected with Trieste, Venice, Ravenna and Ancona.

Three ships currently arrive at Rijeka Gateway weekly: one mother vessel on the Asia–Europe service and two smaller feeder vessels. The introduction of an additional feeder service for Ploče and Durrës is expected soon. The terminal has also started parallel operations, which means that two smaller feeder vessels, around 150 metres in length, can be berthed in parallel at the terminal, and operations on them take place in parallel, which enables better utilisation of the operational quay, shorter waiting times for ships and greater efficiency of terminal operations.

“Rijeka has always had a vision and the port has always been the one that carried new development moments. We are striving for the connection of the Port of Rijeka with a double-track railway to go as quickly as possible, and for the container terminals to get an exit with the most efficient part of extracting traffic from the port. This port is not only a local and national interest, it has always been a European hub, and Rijeka Gateway contributes precisely to such positioning of Rijeka,” said Nina Perko, Director of the Maritime Administration in the Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure.

Denis Vukorepa, Director of the Port Authority of Rijeka, recalled that thanks to Rijeka Gateway the total container traffic in the Port of Rijeka in the first six months of this year increased by 66 percent, and total traffic by around 40 percent.

“A year ago here we spoke about what Rijeka Gateway would mean for Rijeka, Croatia and this transport route. Today we see concrete results. In less than a year the terminal has received its hundredth ship, opened more than 420 new jobs and confirmed that Rijeka is once again strongly written on the map of European and world logistical flows. Rijeka Gateway represents the foundation for the further development of the port and an important step forward for the economy of Rijeka and Croatia,” said Denis Vukorepa, Director of the Port Authority of Rijeka.

“Rijeka has always been connected with the port, the port is part of our identity and part of our future. That is why it is important to us that our port is competitive, well connected with European and world markets. We are especially pleased that the development of the terminal brings new jobs, new knowledge, and especially opportunities for young people and the fact that young people can build their knowledge and experience right in our city. We want a Rijeka that develops, attracts such investments, creates new opportunities, new jobs, but a city in which development takes place with respect for space and the quality of life of our citizens,” emphasised Vedran Vivoda, Deputy Mayor of the City of Rijeka.

The terminal has received more than a thousand trains and over 80 thousand trucks since opening, and the current ratio of cargo transport from the terminal is 42 percent by rail and 58 percent by road.

corridors, ecology and employees

During the first year of terminal operations, more than 92 thousand hours of education and professional training were invested in employee development. This was preceded by an intensive period of learning and preparation, during which in 2025, ahead of the terminal’s launch, 130 thousand hours of education were recorded.

“When we draw a line under the first year of operations, I must say that I am most proud of three things. The first is our team of 422 employees, and that a young team considering that the average age of employees is 35 years, but also a team in which 20 percent are women, employed in almost all functions and levels of management. In Rijeka, and even in the wider region, such a technologically advanced terminal did not exist, our jobs and processes are special and very complex, so building a team that can compete at that level with the best terminals is a source of pride not only for all of us at Rijeka Gateway, but also for Rijeka and the whole of Croatia.

The second are the new logistical corridors with which we have connected Rijeka with the region, which is a great value that our terminal has brought. The third is that we have continued to carefully monitor our impact on the environment and the community with the goal of being a good neighbour to the citizens of Rijeka. We have successfully certified the environmental management system according to the ISO 14001:2015 standard, confirming our commitment to environmental protection, and we continuously communicate with the local community on all topics related to the quality of life of citizens,” said Peter Corfitsen, President of the Management Board of Rijeka Gateway.

The terminal has received more than a thousand trains and over 80 thousand trucks since opening, and the current ratio of cargo transport from the terminal is 42 percent by rail and 58 percent by road. The entry and exit process for truck transport is fully digitised, which speeds up the truck processing process and reduces waiting times, which reduces the burden on traffic and pollution. The average truck time is around 15 minutes, and the shortest achieved truck processing time is ten minutes, and that on a day when more than 500 trucks were processed.

It is clear that the main limitation remains the railway. In this year little has changed. Nevertheless, information indicates that the project has finally received the long-desired “acceleration”, primarily bureaucratic. The project practically languished unprepared for years, only to receive the necessary acceleration in the past year. Processes have been moved from a standstill, so it is still to be expected that by the middle of the next decade we will finally see the realisation of that project.

investments for rijeka and the community

“By handling 370 thousand TEU of cargo we have significantly raised the total capacity of the Port of Rijeka and we are rapidly approaching the numbers we planned – and that is to reach a handling of 650 thousand TEU, and then in the second phase one million TEU. During the first year of operations Rijeka Gateway maintained a high level of operational reliability, with 98 percent availability of port equipment and 99 percent availability of key systems on the operational quay and storage areas, which is at the level of the best terminals.

For the full potential of the terminal, the planned increase in the capacity of rail traffic will be key and here we welcome the activities of the Government of the Republic of Croatia. We will continue to invest in the local community, especially through cooperation with the Faculty of Maritime Studies and the University of Rijeka, through various scholarship and education programmes, but also through donation programmes aimed at Rijeka kindergartens and primary schools,” concluded Tomislav Rosandić, Member of the Management Board of Rijeka Gateway.

World.title: Iraq reviews work with foreign banks, credit rating with Rothschild & Co.
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Edouard de Rothschild of Rothschild & Co. discussed on Monday cooperation with international banks and strategies to improve Iraq’s credit rating.

During their meeting in the French capital, Paris, the two sides discussed approaches to expand Iraq’s cooperation with foreign banks, as well as the Iraqi government’s efforts to develop the banking sector, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The discussions also focused on the Iraqi government’s objectives in building a strong and diversified economy.

Rothschild highlighted Iraq’s investment potential and the approaches in which foreign financial institutions might contribute to the country’s development objectives.

The prime minister’s meeting with Rothschild is part of his diplomatic agenda in Paris. Al-Zaidi also met with French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace to discuss regional security and energy supply channels.

Al-Zaidi held a separate meeting with TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanne to discuss a multibillion-dollar expansion of Iraq’s oil and gas production capability.

Following his trip to France, the Iraqi prime minister is planned to fly to the German capital, Berlin, to continue his European tour.

World.title: Three talking points from the Spanish Grand Prix
World.content:
Madrid – Eight wins, the most by an Italian driver in a single season, and blessed with good fortune as well as extreme talent, it is no longer a question of if Kimi Antonelli will win the drivers’ world championship, but when?

In a season of uncertain length, with the final two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi remaining in doubt, there are various permutations in terms of the points likely to be required for an unassailable advantage.

As Antonelli closes in on becoming Italy’s first champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, AFP Sport looks at three talking points from Sunday’s processional Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit:

More records ready to be broken by Antonelli

The 20-year-old prodigy from Bologna already has a lead of 81 points ahead of his Mercedes team-mate George Russell, who has abandoned talking of his own title bid.

If the season includes a two-race finale in the Middle East, where the US-Israeli war with Iran makes this doubtful, he will need 153 points, from the 233 available, to become champion.

A total of 152 might be enough, thanks to his tie-breaking supremacy in number of race wins -– offering up the prospect of Antonelli taking his maiden title in Singapore next month.

But if the season is reduced from 23 races to 22 with a final race taking place at Imola, close to Antonelli’s home town, on December 6, a reduced maximum of 208 points will be on offer and the target falls to 127 –- which may be achievable in Mexico on November 1.

If he succeeded in Mexico, he would take the title aged 20 years, two months and eight days — thus reducing the record for youngest world champion held by four-time champion Sebastian Vettel by three years.

Norris’s bad luck with safety rules

World champion Lando Norris described himself as “insanely unlucky” not to win Sunday’s race as a result of the timing of a Virtual Safety Car (VSC) that was called seconds after he passed the pit lane entry.

It cost him a “cheap” pit stop and handed the initiative to his rivals, Charles Leclerc of Ferrari and Antonelli, who waited for the Monegasque driver to make his essential pit-stop before seizing victory with aplomb.

Antonelli and others pitted during the VSC, saving time and gaining an approximate 20-seconds advantage on Norris who had to fight back from fifth to finish third behind four-time champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull.

It was clearly unfair on Norris to be penalised for being the fastest driver on track and leading at the time when Lance Stroll lost control of his Aston Martin and went into the barriers.

“It is a rule that should not define a whole race,” said Norris. “I was the only one on the whole grid that didn’t get the chance to do the pit stop.”

His McLaren team boss Andrea Stella said: “Perhaps there’s a wider reflection that the F1 community should apply, as to whether you keep things like they are — or you introduce ways of maintaining more fairness.”

Honda make changes

Fernando Alonso was more than two seconds off the pace when he was eliminated from qualifying at his home race on Saturday, a clear sign his Honda-powered Aston Martin was lacking power.

As the two-time world champion publicly ponders his future, Honda announced a change of leadership for their engine programme. It may, however, be too late to persuade Alonso to stay for another year.

World.title: Germany seeks guarantees from Italy’s UniCredit over Commerzbank takeover
World.content:
Frankfurt – Germany’s finance minister was due on Monday to meet the UniCredit CEO to seek guarantees over the future of Commerzbank, as the Italian lender gears up to complete a takeover of its German rival.

Lars Klingbeil would urge UniCredit boss Andrea Orcel to protect jobs in Germany and ensure Commerzbank remains a key lender to the country’s small- and medium-sized businesses, Berlin said.

Despite fierce resistance from Berlin and the German lender, UniCredit has built up a stake of nearly 50 percent in Commerzbank and is close to sealing one of Europe’s biggest banking mergers in recent years.

A German finance ministry spokesman conceded the banks had moved into a “a different phase now” and were negotiating a transaction.

But he stressed Klingbeil wanted to ensure Commerzbank’s interests and the country’s were protected during the talks in Berlin.

“Commerzbank has over 40,000 employees and we naturally want to safeguard their interests,” he told a press conference.

Commerzbank’s “core business model” in financing Germany’s small businesses, which form the backbone of Europe’s biggest economy, should be preserved too, he said.

It was also key that Commerzbank’s main operations remained in Frankfurt to ensure the city continued as “one of the most important financial centres in Europe,” the spokesman said.

– Banking behemoth –

Berlin still believes it has some influence over the deal through its representation on Commerzbank’s supervisory board and its roughly 12-percent stake in the bank, both legacies of a state bailout during the financial crisis.

But its leverage is now likely to be diminished given the size of UniCredit’s stake.

UniCredit started building up its holding in Commerzbank in 2024 in a bid to launch a takeover.

Commerzbank slashed thousands of jobs and hiked its financial targets in an effort to convince shareholders to back its campaign to remain independent.

But these efforts failed and, with UniCredit closing in on a controlling stake, Commerzbank’s CEO Bettina Orlopp called in late July for “constructive” talks with the Italian lender.

UniCredit wants to create a European banking behemoth better able to take on bigger US rivals and argues that a merger would strengthen the region’s fragmented banking sector.

Despite resistance in Germany, some policymakers in Brussels and at the European Central Bank have been more supportive of a possible takeover.

World.title: Saudi football body vows action against Jota chants, Ronaldo urges life ban
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabian football authorities promised to take action and Cristiano Ronaldo called for life bans after rival fans taunted Al-Hilal’s Ruben Neves about the death of Diogo Jota, his friend and former Portugal team-mate.

Chants about Jota, the Liverpool and Portugal forward who died in a car crash last year, rang out during Al-Hilal’s 6-0 away win over Al-Taawoun on Saturday.

“The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour,” Saudi-based Portugal captain Ronaldo wrote on Instagram on Sunday.

“People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again,” he added.

Midfielder Neves, 29, reacted to the chants coming from the stands by sarcastically giving a thumbs-up and applauding, before pointing towards the sky.

“I just hope they don’t go to pray later after what they did,” he said after the match.

Neves was one of Jota’s closest friends and was a pallbearer at his funeral. Jota, 28, and his brother Andre, 25, died in a crash in Spain in July 2025.

The Saudi Arabian Football Federation and Saudi Pro League condemned “unacceptable conduct by some supporters” in a joint statement late on Sunday.

“Exploiting personal tragedies for the purpose of abuse or provocation is unacceptable behaviour that has no place in Saudi football,” the statement said.

“Relevant committees have identified the conduct in question and will take the necessary action in accordance with the applicable regulations and procedures,” it added.

Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 World Cup, one of the flagship events underpinning its drive to diversify an economy still heavily dependent on oil.

The powerful Gulf monarchy has invested nearly two billion dollars in football over three years, attracting stars such as Ronaldo, Neymar and Karim Benzema.

World.title: IFC appoints Thomas Jacobs to lead Iraq and regional private sector investment
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The International Finance Corporation has selected Thomas Jacobs as its new Division Director for Iraq, the Levant, and Yemen, overseeing the World Bank Group’s private-sector development efforts in the area.

Jacobs will take over IFC efforts in Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, the West Bank, and Gaza, following Khawaja Aftab Ahmed after four years in the role.

Based in Amman, Jacobs will collaborate with governments, companies, and development partners to increase private capital and employment growth.

His top priority will be infrastructure investment, access to credit for small and medium-sized enterprises, digitalization, and water security, as well as establishing conditions for increased private-sector engagement.

These sectors are especially important for Iraq as it strives to attract more international investment, diversify its oil-dependent economy, and give private enterprises a bigger role in infrastructure and jobs.

Jacobs joined the World Bank Group in 2003 and has held several senior roles in the Middle East and Asia.

He previously worked in Cairo and Beirut and most recently served as temporary division director for East Asia and the Pacific after a stint as country manager in Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia.

IFC is the World Bank Group’s private-sector arm, offering investment and consultancy services targeted at mobilizing private resources in emerging countries.

World.title: TotalEnergies to raise investments in Iraq to $16 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chairman and CEO of TotalEnergies, Patrick Pouyanne, stated on Monday that the company’s investments in Iraq’s oil and gas sectors are currently valued at $12 billion, with intentions to increase this amount to $16 billion in the future.

Pouyanne’s remarks took place during his meeting with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi in Paris, where they reviewed the company’s strategic projects in Iraq, particularly in the gas sector, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi detailed the government’s strategies to improve the recovery of associated gas and achieve self-sufficiency. He also discussed plans to boost oil production over the next five years, aiming for Iraq to reach a production target of 10 million barrels per day.

The prime minister noted that efforts are underway to broaden the scope of oil exploration in Iraq to benefit the national economy and support development objectives.

Al-Zaidi also mentioned that preparations are ongoing to organize an international energy conference in Baghdad.

Pouyanne underlined TotalEnergies’ readiness to collaborate with Iraq in the energy industries.

The French company’s commitment to its projects in Iraq highlights the significance of the Iraqi market within the framework of the European energy strategy.

This significance is especially relevant as major corporations navigate the risks posed by regional tensions while investing in one of the richest oil producers in the region.

World.title: Nigerian oil refinery Dangote launches IPO
World.content:
Lagos – Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote on Monday launched what is slated as Africa’s biggest initial public offering (IPO), which aims to raise $1.6 billion to expand his mega oil refinery to become the world’s largest.

The Lagos-based refinery, which began operations in 2024, has a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day, exceeding domestic demand in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.

It began exporting its fuel abroad a few months ago.

The Dangote Petroleum Refinery aims to raise funds to double its capacity to 1.4 million barrels a day by 2028, which would make it the world’s largest refinery, surpassing Jamnagar in India.

Describing it as an “historic day”, Dangote said in a statement that the IPO was “not simply about listing a company. It is about listing a new possibility for Nigeria, and for Africa”.

Investors can buy as few as 10 shares at 525 naira each, potentially raising 2.15 trillion naira ($1.6 billion) in a move Dangote hopes will give ordinary people a chance for a stake in a long-term asset.

He has said the offering, which closes October 13, will be the biggest IPO in African history and has encouraged participation by small investors, including people on lower incomes.

Dangote also plans to build a 700,000 barrel-per-day east African oil refinery in Lamu, on the Kenyan coast.

World.title: Houthis target Saudi base as Iran denies involvement in Yemen war
World.content:
Sanaa – Yemen’s Houthis launched a fresh barrage of missile and drone attacks on Saudi military targets on Monday, as Iran denied any involvement in the country’s revived civil war.

The group, fighting the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government, last week seized control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which has become vital as the wider US-Iran war chokes the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis said they fired dozens of drones and missiles at the kingdom, prompting the Saudi Civil Defence to issue brief alerts in the neighbouring cities of Khamis Mushait and Abha.

A Khamis Mushait resident told AFP he heard “intense blasts” which left fires burning for a “long time”.

“Honestly, we couldn’t sleep at all.”

The Bab al-Mandab waterway has become essential for Saudi oil exports, with Iran continuing to block the Hormuz strait as part of the Middle East war, but the Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on Riyadh.

The renewed fighting in Yemen comes as the wider regional war remains stalemated. On Monday, a proposed meeting between Gulf states and Iran over the future of Hormuz was postponed, with Tehran accusing Riyadh of using Yemen as a “pretext” to delay the talks.

Tehran has long supported the Houthis, a member of its anti-Israel “axis of resistance, including with weapons and technology, but analysts dispute the extent to which Iran is behind the renewed fighting.

“Iran does not interfere in Yemeni affairs,” foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters on Monday, saying the Houthis are “entirely independent actors who make their decisions based on their own interests”.

Iran has previously threatened to open “new fronts”, including Bab al-Mandab, and the Houthi offensive has sent oil prices soaring once again, with the lengthy route through the Suez Canal and around Africa now the only secure route for Saudi oil to reach key Asian markets.

– 300 strikes in five days –

Yemen’s prolonged civil war had been dormant for four years before bursting back into life in July over an Iranian flight to the capital Sanaa, as it became the latest conflict drawn into the wider regional war.

The Houthis’ military spokesman Yahya Saree said Monday that the group’s latest strikes targeted “fighter jet hangars, radars, runways, ammunition depots” at King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait, in retaliation for airstrikes by Riyadh.

He accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out “more than 300 airstrikes in the past five days” across Yemen.

Yemeni government forces on Sunday said they had recaptured positions in the southwestern province of Taiz from Houthi fighters and carried out airstrikes, telling the official Saba news agency they killed at least ten gunmen.

Last week, American media reported that US President Donald Trump had rejected a personal request from Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the kingdom’s de facto ruler, to intervene in the war.

The Saudi crown prince received the commander of the US Central Command, Admiral Brad Cooper, in Jeddah on Monday to discuss “the latest developments in the region”, according to Saudi news agency SPA.

The US admiral travelled to Saudi Arabia on Thursday for urgent coordination meetings, according to US news site Axios.

The Houthis, whose heartland is among Yemen’s Zaidi Muslims in the country’s north, seized the capital Sanaa in 2014 at the outset of the civil war, driving the government to Aden in the south.

The following year, Saudi Arabia led a coalition to intervene on the side of the government, launching wave after wave of airstrikes as the conflict escalated into one of the worst humanitarian disasters in the world.

In 2025, the United Nations warned that 17 million Yemenis were struggling to eat and a further million faced extreme hunger.

On Sunday, the UN’s migration agency said the renewed fighting in the Arab world’s poorest country had forced 86,000 people to flee their homes, with the number jumping by 10,000 in just a day.

More than 2,000 people had fled across the Bab al-Mandab to reach Djibouti in Africa, the International Organization for Migration said.

World.title: 'Ensure actual resolution, don't just formally close complaints': Uttarakhand CM Dhami warns officials during CM Helpline 1905 review
World.content:
DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister

on Monday reviewed the functioning of the CM Helpline 1905 at the Secretariat and directed officials to ensure the swift, time-bound and satisfactory resolution of public grievances.

The chief minister said that the CM Helpline is an important mechanism for addressing the problems of the common people. He stressed that grievance redressal should not be limited to formally closing complaints on the portal, but must ensure an actual resolution of the complainant's problem.

Dhami directed district magistrates to review complaints department-wise in districts where a particular category of grievances is being received in large numbers and ensure their early resolution.

He also called for an analysis of the reasons behind repeated complaints of the same nature and effective measures to address such issues permanently.

The chief minister directed all district magistrates to conduct surprise inspections of tehsils. During these inspections, special attention should be paid to whether mutation-related cases are being disposed of within the prescribed timelines. He said complaints related to land fraud should be addressed on priority. The chief minister stressed that people should not be made to make unnecessary visits to government offices for revenue-related matters and that prescribed services must be delivered within the stipulated time

Dhami directed officials to accord top priority to ensuring the availability of clean drinking water.





He said complaints related to drinking water should be acted upon immediately. He directed the concerned officials to conduct an audit of water pipelines and sewer lines within 15 days and submit a report. Timely resolution of disruptions in water supply, leakages and other related issues should be ensured.

The chief minister directed officials to pay special attention to grievances pending for more than 30 days.

Secretaries, heads of departments and district magistrates should regularly review pending complaints at their respective levels. Accountability should be fixed for officials in cases where complaints are not resolved within the prescribed timeframe.

He further directed that long-pending complaints be resolved on the highest priority. During the meeting, a department-wise status of complaints pending for more than 180 days was also presented.

Dhami said such old cases should be regularly monitored at the departmental level and the reasons for their pendency should also be reviewed.

The chief minister instructed officials not to close complaints unnecessarily under "Special Close" or "Force Close" categories. He said the satisfaction of complainants must be given due importance in grievance redressal. Before closing any complaint, officials must ensure that all necessary action has been taken at the appropriate level to resolve the issue.

Dhami said the feedback mechanism for complaints received through the CM Helpline should be further strengthened. The quality of grievance redressal should be assessed on the basis of feedback received from complainants. The portal has provisions for obtaining public feedback and monitoring the action being taken by various departments and nodal officers.

The chief minister said officials and personnel performing well in grievance redressal should be encouraged, while accountability should be fixed for those found guilty of unnecessary delays or negligence.

He said the fundamental objective of the CM Helpline is to establish effective communication between the government and the public and ensure real, time-bound and satisfactory resolution of citizens' problems.

During the review, the chief minister also spoke to several complainants over the phone to ascertain the actual status of their grievances and their redressal.

Dhami spoke to Sanjay Kumar Rawat regarding a complaint that had been closed inappropriately.

Rawat informed him that medical reimbursement bills related to the treatment of his late father had not been paid. The chief minister directed the concerned officials to take immediate necessary action and ensure payment of the pending medical reimbursement. He said people should not be unnecessarily harassed in such sensitive cases and warned that accountability would be fixed if similar complaints arise in the future.

The chief minister also spoke to Baby Kotnala, a resident of Pauri Garhwal, regarding her issue related to destitute women's pension. She informed him that despite registering a complaint a long time ago, the issue had not been resolved. Dhami directed the District Magistrate, Pauri Garhwal, to take immediate appropriate action and ensure resolution of the matter.

World.title: Yogi Adityanath announces welfare measures, tech push for lawyers in UP
World.content:
PRAYAGRAJ: Chief minister

on Monday took a swipe at the previous Samajwadi Party government, saying that before 2017, the state faced not only a shortage of resources but also issues related to governance, transparency, accountability, law and order, and judicial infrastructure.

Additionally, the chief minister revealed plans to provide tablets to 400 state law officers to equip them with modern technology, enabling them to access information on government-related cases before the courts.

In another announcement, Adityanath said the state government would introduce a cashless insurance scheme providing coverage of up to Rs 5 lakh for practising advocates in

.

Addressing a felicitation ceremony organised by the Allahabad High Court Bar Association here, Adityanath said nearly 45 to 50 per cent posts in the Uttar Pradesh Police were vacant before his government assumed office in 2017.

"Before 2017, the challenge before us was not merely of resources. It was also a challenge of the system and approach, transparency and accountability in administration, law and order and judicial infrastructure," the chief minister said.

He highlighted that the police force's annual training capacity at that time was only about 3,000 personnel but has now increased to 60,000.

"There was no training capacity and even basic facilities for the police were lacking," Adityanath said, adding that his government has strengthened police infrastructure and training facilities across the state.





Adityanath also addressed the condition of the subordinate judiciary before 2017, pointing out that many courts operated in dilapidated or temporary buildings, and that district courts in as many as ten districts functioned from rented premises.

Furthermore, he stated that his government had also addressed several shortcomings that earlier hampered the criminal justice system, including witnesses turning hostile out of fear in serious criminal cases and inadequate arrangements for transporting prisoners from jails to courts.

"Today, you can see the results of better coordination between the executive and the judiciary. When we reform and transform, the performance becomes visible on its own," the chief minister said.

He emphasised that a robust judiciary strengthens the foundations of good governance, which should be the top priority of any elected government.

Adityanath noted hat his government has prioritised greater use of technology, modernised infrastructure, and improved coordination between police and prosecution, leading to significant increases in conviction rates.

He pointed out that the prosecution system is now connected to online platforms to ensure timely charge sheet filings and effective presentations of scientific evidence in court.

Referring to emerging challenges, Adityanath said the legal fraternity must prepare itself for areas ranging from cybercrime and artificial intelligence to data privacy, e-commerce, fintech, intellectual property and climate litigation.

"A future-ready Bar will lay a strong foundation for a future-ready justice system," he said, adding that the younger generation of lawyers has a major responsibility in carrying forward the rich traditions of the Allahabad High Court.

The chief minister said that district courts and jails have been provided with high-speed internet and video conferencing facilities. Additionally, the virtual recording of evidence and the digitization of court documents are being promoted to reduce trial delays.

"Justice delayed is justice denied," he said, stressing that timely and impartial justice was essential to maintaining public faith in the judiciary and other democratic institutions.

Integrated court complexes were being developed to provide judicial facilities, residential accommodation for judicial officers, chambers for lawyers and other amenities under one roof, he said.

World.title: You can run, but can't escape law: Mann warns gangsters
World.content:
Punjab Chief Minister

on Monday said his government adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards gangsters, extortionists, drug traffickers and organised criminal networks, irrespective of how powerful or well-connected they may claim to be.

He further asserted that law and order is fully maintained in Punjab and there is no haven for criminals.

Felicitating the Punjab Police team led by Superintendent of Police, Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF), Bikramjit Singh Brar, for securing the extradition of notorious fugitive criminal Amritpal Singh alias Amrit Dalam from the Republic of Moldova, the chief minister said the government is fully committed to Punjab's peace and security.

Dalam was detained by the Moldovan authorities on February 24 while trying to cross the Otaci state border to Ukraine. Subsequently, the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC) of the Punjab Police began an extradition process to bring him to India.

Mann highlighted that 1,234 gangster modules have been busted and 10 fugitives deported from abroad, while 60,582 FIRs have been registered against drug traffickers and properties worth Rs 366 crore seized.





He highlighted that the Punjab Police is equipped with high-tech anti-drone systems and Village Defence Committees comprising 1.5 lakh people have been formed, warning that no person or group attempting to disturb Punjab's peace will be spared.

Felicitating the police officers for their exemplary achievement, Mann said, "The successful extradition sends an unequivocal message to gangsters, criminals and their handlers operating from foreign soil that Punjab Police will chase them across borders and bring them back to face the law."

Gangsters cannot find a haven for themselves anymore. Whether they are hiding in Punjab, another part of India or thousands of kilometres away in Europe, the Punjab Police will track them down. They may change their locations, passports and identities, but they cannot escape the law forever, the chief minister said.

Extradition of Amrit Dalam is a major achievement in Punjab's relentless campaign against organised crime and demonstrates the effectiveness of the state government's 'Gangstran Te Vaar' campaign, Mann stated.

"Amrit Dalam was a key operative of the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria Gang and was wanted in several serious criminal cases, including murder, attempt to murder, offences under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, Arms Act and narcotic offence," he added.

Mann appreciated the coordinated efforts of the GTF, Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC), Punjab Police and central agencies, saying that close inter-agency coordination has emerged as a powerful weapon in dismantling transnational criminal networks.

During its recent visit to Moldova, the Punjab Police team received a token of appreciation from the government of the Republic of Moldova in recognition of the close coordination and cooperation that facilitated the first-ever extradition of a fugitive criminal from Moldova to India.

Describing the gesture as a matter of pride for Punjab, Mann said, "This recognition reflects the mutual trust, respect and growing law-enforcement cooperation between India and Moldova.

This is not merely an award or a token. It is recognition of the professional capabilities of Punjab Police and the trust that international law-enforcement agencies are placing in our officers."

Mann expressed pride in how the Punjab Police have demonstrated professionalism and determination, even when criminals attempt to create an international shield around themselves.

The successful extradition further illustrates that the Punjab Police will continue to pursue organised criminals beyond geographical boundaries, ensuring that those wanted for serious crimes are brought back to face justice, the chief minister stated.

World.title: 3 Italian passengers fly out of Delhi without immigration clearance: What exactly happened
World.content:
3 Italian passengers flew from Amritsar to Munich without immigration clearance

What exactly happened?

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The civil aviation ministry has issued a show-cause notice to Air India over alleged procedural lapses that allowed three Italian passengers to board a connecting flight from Delhi without completing immigration formalities earlier this month.The notice has been issued to the Air India CEO.The home ministry has also convened a meeting of stakeholders on Tuesday to discuss the incident, sources told news agency PTI.The three passengers flew from Amritsar to Delhi on September 4 before boarding a Lufthansa flight to Munich from Delhi airport. However, they did not complete the required immigration formalities at the airport, sources added.Titled âviolation of SOP for hub and spoke operations resulting in three foreign nationals departing India without mandatory immigration clearance,â the show-cause notice issued to Air India last Saturday said the three passengers arrived in Delhi from Amritsar on AI 1115 at 12.50 am on September 4 and subsequently departed for Munich on a codeshare Lufthansa flight at 1.45 am, within an hour of their arrival.Home secretary Govind Mohan will chair a meeting on Tuesday to discuss the incident.The secretary and additional secretary of the civil aviation ministry, Intelligence Bureau director, additional secretary (UT and Foreigners) of the home ministry, Bureau of Immigration commissioner, Air India CEO and Delhi airport CEO are expected to attend the meeting, they added.Amritsar airport is among the airports where Air India operates flights under its âHub-and-Spokeâ model.Under this arrangement, passengers complete immigration formalities at the airport of origin and can then travel to an overseas destination through a designated hub. At the hub airport, where the international flight departs, passengers are required only to undergo security checks before boarding.For a passenger travelling from Amritsar via Delhi to an international destination, Amritsar serves as the spoke and Delhi as the hub.In the case of the three Italian passengers, sources said they were issued boarding passes at Amritsar for both their flight to Delhi and the Lufthansa flight to Munich.However, as the two flights were not covered under Air Indiaâs âHub-and-Spokeâ model, the passengers were required to exit through the arrival area at Delhi and complete immigration formalities before taking the Lufthansa flight.After arriving at Delhi airport, they were instead taken to the international transfer area and did not reach the immigration counter. They then boarded the flight to Munich without completing the immigration process, the sources said, as cited by PTI.Air India and Lufthansa have an interline partnership. An interline agreement generally allows passengers to book connecting flights operated by different airlines under a single itinerary.

World.title: Nearly 50 lakh hit by floods in Bihar as swollen rivers breach danger marks
World.content:
Nearly 50 lakh people across 15 districts of Bihar have been affected by floods as heavy rain in recent days caused rivers already flowing above danger levels to swell further, officials said on Monday.

Bihar has recorded 112.7 mm of rainfall so far this month, about six per cent above normal, according to the local weather office.

According to the Disaster Management Department, floods have affected 49.67 lakh people across 15 districts in Bihar.

The affected districts include Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnea, Madhepura and Araria.

An official said incessant rain in the catchment areas of rivers flowing from Nepal into Bihar, along with heavy rainfall in the state, has pushed several rivers and streams above their danger marks, as cited by PTI.

The Ganga was flowing at 36.19 metres at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur at 6.00 pm on Monday, 1.69 metres above the danger level.

The Kosi river was flowing above the danger mark at Baltara and Kursela, while the Budhi Gandak had crossed the danger level at Khagaria.





The Ganga was above the danger mark at Digha, Gandhi Ghat, Hathidah, Bhagalpur, Kahalgaon and Munger. The Punpun at Sripalpur, Bagmati at Benibad and Ghaghara at Darauli were also flowing above their respective danger levels.

The administration has set up 1,248 community kitchens and 13 relief camps in the flood-hit areas. Around 11,508 people have been provided accommodation, food, medical care and other essential facilities, officials said.

The Disaster Management Department said the Gandak barrage at Valmiki Nagar recorded a water discharge of 1,09,000 cusecs at 4 pm on Monday, with the flow continuing to rise.

At the Kosi Barrage in Birpur, the discharge stood at 1,63,315 cusecs, against this year's highest flow of 2,55,425 cusecs recorded on July 20.

Twenty-seven teams of the State Disaster Response Force and 10 teams of the National Disaster Response Force have been deployed across various districts for relief and rescue operations.

World.title: ‘Partners, not rivals’: China FM Wang Yi reveals key PM Modi-Xi consensus
World.content:
18th BRICS Summit in Delhi

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India and China should view each other as partners rather than rivals, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi said on Monday, citing the consensus reached between president Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Narendra Modi during their meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi.Wang said the two leaders held a âcandid and in-depth exchange of viewsâ on strategic and long-term issues concerning bilateral ties, according to news agency PTI. âThe most important consensus they reached was that China and India should be partners,â he told Chinese official media.According to Wang, Xi said China and India could draw on each other's strengths, support one another, help each other succeed and pursue common development. The two leaders also agreed to maintain peace and tranquillity in border areas and support each other during their respective BRICS chairmanships.The Chinese foreign ministry said the relationship had moved from a ârestartâ to a ârenewed elevationâ under the strategic guidance of the two leaders. Wang said areas of cooperation were expanding, trade had reached record levels and people-to-people exchanges were becoming more active.Wang also quoted PM Modi as saying India was ready to be âa partner, not an adversaryâ to China and viewed each otherâs development âas an opportunity rather than a challengeâ. He said PM had reaffirmed that Indiaâs approach to China was independent of third-party influence.The two leaders, according to Wang, agreed to deepen political trust, appropriately manage differences and strengthen cooperation in areas including cultural exchanges and direct air connectivity. They also agreed to coordinate more closely through the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and the G20, while advancing cooperation among Global South countries.The Indian foreign ministryâs account of the meeting highlighted the need for a âstrategic and long-term perspectiveâ in managing bilateral ties. According to MEA, PM Modi said differences should not become disputes and that relations should be guided by âthree mutualsâ â mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest.PM Modi also stressed that peace and tranquillity along the border remained essential for the broader relationship and called for adherence to existing agreements and understandings. Both sides backed a âfair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolutionâ of the boundary question.On trade, the leaders discussed structural imbalances, supply-chain concerns and the need for âmeaningful and predictable market accessâ. They also welcomed progress in people-to-people ties and called for greater cultural, business and travel links.Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing would work with New Delhi to implement the understandings reached by the leaders and âmake the cooperation list longerâ.She said, "As the two leaders have charted the course for the future development of the bilateral ties, China will work with India to implement the important common understandings reached between the two leaders."With China set to assume the BRICS chairmanship in 2027, both sides are expected to build on the latest engagement.

,

The plea had challenged the Maharashtra FDA's August 11 notices over allegations that s for Vimal Elaichi amounted to surrogate promotion of Vimal Pan Masala, a chewable product banned in Maharashtra.

Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma had reserved the order after hearing arguments on whether the Delhi High Court had territorial jurisdiction to entertain the petition.

âThe government of Maharashtra, which has passed the show-cause notice, is not here to defend its show-cause notice,â counsel Rukhmini Bobde had submitted.

World.title: Mother dies a day after voting, son wins Rajasthan civic poll by just 1 vote
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In Rajasthan local body polls, a single vote decided the fate of an Independent candidate Jagdish Prasad as he defeated BJP's Ramsharan by the narrowest possible margin, securing 151 votes against his rival's 150, as news agency IANS reported.

Coincidentally, mother of the Independent candidate contesting from Ward No. 6 died a day after casting her ballot in the polls.

With just one vote separating the two candidates, every single ballot proved decisive. Even a vote would have reversed the result, making the Jagdish Prasad's mother ballot especially significant for the family.

Residents have also been discussing the timing of the two events, with the narrow electoral victory coming just a day after his mother's final vote.

The Ward No. 6 contest stood out amid the municipal election results because of its exceptionally close finish. Jagdish Prasad's 151 votes were enough to take the seat, while Ramsharan fell just one vote short.

Jagdish Prasad's victory as an Independent over a BJP candidate has also drawn attention in the ward.

World.title: China’s spy chief warns of national security risks from AI
World.content:
The head of China's spy agency has warned that artificial intelligence endangers the country's national security, with foreign powers potentially using the technology to threaten social order.

"Hostile forces" were abusing generative AI technologies to "fabricate political rumours and spread harmful information", Minister of State Security Chen Yixin wrote in an article published online on Sunday (September 13, 2026).

"They launch public opinion wars and cognitive warfare against China, directly threatening our political security, institutional security and ideological security," he said.

The warning comes as Chinese leader Xi Jinping is due to meet U.S. President Donald Trump in Washington this month, with AI governance and safety set to be part of their discussions as calls mount for greater oversight of the technology.

U.S. tech leaders have also called for slowing AI advances.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned on Saturday of the "reckless" speed of AI technology development, as worries mount over the risks of superintelligent computer systems.

OpenAI boss Sam Altman said he agreed with Mr. Amodei's assessment.

But Mr. Chen warned that AI was now "the main battleground for global technological competition and a new track for major power strategic rivalry".

Risks to China's critical information infrastructure

He did not mention existential risks or putting the brakes on technological advances, but singled out Anthropic's Claude Mythos and OpenAI's ChatGPT-5.5-Cyber for their advanced hacking capabilities that potentially "pose serious risks to China's critical information infrastructure".

"Foreign intelligence agencies are deeply using technologies such as intelligent web crawlers, intelligent data mining, and intelligent profiling analysis to extensively collect and acquire sensitive information such as key national data, trade secrets, and citizens' personal privacy," Mr. Chen said.

The U.S.-Iran war has also demonstrated AI's key role in the military, with better technology offering battlefield advantages, he said.

China must "ensure independent control of key core technologies" - including the advanced computer chips vital to training AI models - to secure its technology sovereignty, Mr. Chen wrote.

World.title: 17 of 20 NCPI MPs to likely to join BJP, says MP Jagadish Basunia
World.content:
Trinamool Congress MP from Cooch Behar Jagdish Chandra Barma Basunia, who along with 19 other MPs of the party defected to National Citizens Party of India (NCPI), on Monday (September 14, 2026) said that 17 MPs of NCPI are likely to join the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) before Durga Puja in October this year.

“Now we have no hurdle in joining BJP. Three MPs do not want to join the BJP, they will remain with NCPI. The remaining 17 of us will join with BJP before the pujas,” Mr. Basunia told media persons at Cooch Behar.

The three MPs not willing to join the BJP are Abu Taher Khan, Khalilur Rahman and Yusuf Pathan, who have gone on record to say that they will not join the BJP.

Mr. Basunia said that all the rebel MPs of the Trinamool wanted to join the BJP directly but there was a ‘little problem’ as the three minority MPs did not want to join the party directly and that was the reason the MPs merged with NCPI.

Almost a month after the Trinamool Congress lost West Bengal Assembly elections, 20 MPs elected on the Trinamool symbol, on June 14, informed Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla that they had merged with the NCPI, a registered regional political party. All the 20 MPs have offered their support to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government at the Centre.

Meanwhile, leaders in the West Bengal BJP said that they are not aware of any NCPI MPs joining the party.

While the remarks of the Cooch Behar MP triggered speculations in political circles, several MPs of NCPI including senior MPs like Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar and Shatabdi Roy said that they are not aware of any such plans of joining the BJP.

Notably, several NCPI MPs have expressed their wish that they want to join the BJP, but a section of West Bengal BJP leadership is not keen about it. The State BJP leadership is already facing much criticism over allegations of ‘Trinamoolification of the BJP’ — meaning, the saffron party is accommodating leaders and policies of the Trinamool Congress which it fought against.

MP facing protests

The sudden announcement of joining the BJP by Mr. Basunia, a first time MP, is also being attributed to the protests he is facing in Cooch Behar. Mr. Basunia, who was once associated with All India Forward Bloc, has faced repeated protests at home.

A few days ago a rally organised in Cooch Behar witnessed hundreds of people raising ‘Go Back’ slogans against the MP. His wife Sangeeta Basu Basunia, an MLA with the Trinamool Congress, has joined the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction.

World.title: Trump dismisses new AI guardrails, says there is a ’SICK conspiracy’ against AI and data centers
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday (September 14, 2026) that he would be a sufficient guardrail against rogue artificial intelligence, claiming that any efforts to limit the technology was part of a “SICK conspiracy.”

Mr. Trump was pushing back against calls by tech leaders such as Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Elon Musk to have greater government oversight of AI. Their goal is to ensure the technology is developed in ways that promote safety, address legal liability, feed economic growth, advance science and preserve national security.

The president maintained that his presence in the Oval Office should assuage any fears about AI, which has become a source of controversy after a series of hacks in recent months that showed AI agents could be working to deceive humans.

“The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” Mr. Trump posted on social media.

Mr. Trump specifically said that the administration has already stopped the AI company Anthropic “from doing bad, or potentially bad” things. Anthropic has endured an uncomfortable relationship with the Trump administration, with the Pentagon trying to label the company’s models a security risk and a temporary ban of one of its more advanced models.

Mr. Amodei published a 3,800-word essay on Saturday (September 12, 2026) that called for slower development of AI. Microsoft on Monday (September 14, 2026) published its own code of conduct to ensure that humans control AI. The actions come after a series of warnings by AI experts about the technologies’ capabilities and the July 2026 cyberattack by OpenAI models on the AI company Hugging Face.

But the president has opposed such efforts to constrain AI and claims that doing so could cause China to eclipse America on AI.

“There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China,” Mr. Trump said.

The president has long resisted efforts for greater government oversight of AI, embracing his philosophy going back to 2016 of “I alone can fix it.” He returned to the White House last year by revoking a Biden administration executive order on AI oversight and only providing a fuller order of his own more than 16 months later this past June.

The prospect of slower AI buildout led stocks to slip in Monday (September 14, 2026) morning trading, as demand for advanced computer chips and construction materials for data centres could fall. But Mr. Trump’s frustration comes as AI has also emerged as a political liability ahead of November’s midterm elections, with many voters opposing the construction of additional data centres and expressing worries that AI could lead to job losses and undermine the education of children.

Rahm Emanuel, the former Chicago mayor, Democratic congressman and White House chief of staff, said on Saturday (September 12, 2026) that the Anthropic CEO’s essay was “an admission that we’re driving down a dark, winding road on wet pavement with the headlights off. And where’s President Trump? Looks like he nodded off again. It’s time to turn the lights on, put both hands on the wheel, and regain control before it’s too late.”

But the administration has repeatedly sought to minimise the risks being highlighted by AI companies.

Vice-President J.D. Vance told reporters Monday (September 14, 2026) morning about AI, “I don’t think Americans should be scared of anything.”

Mr. Vance, speaking as he prepared to fly to Kansas for a midterm election campaign event, said that the Trump administration is concerned about AI but wants to make sure it is regulating the technology smartly, warning that the U.S. is in an AI arms race against China.

“Personally, I feel a little bit weird about the fact that you have so many frontier AI tech companies kind of coming to the government and begging the government to regulate them. It feels a little bit to me like a bit of a Trojan horse,” Mr. Vance said. “So, I think we just have to be careful about this.”

World.title: Trump says ‘open’ to engaging with Iran
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday (September 14, 2026) he was open to holding talks with Iran, after weeks of saying it was too early to make a deal with Tehran to end the war in West Asia.

"The failing Nation of Iran wants to make a deal, quickly and badly. I will determine whether or not the U.S.A. will choose to engage - The concept of which we are open to," Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network.

Mr. Trump ​reiterated on Sunday ‌(September 13, 2026) that he expected the ​Iran war to ⁠end this year, possibly just after midterm elections ‌due in the United States in November, ‌resulting in a ‌drop ⁠in oil prices.

“Iran ⁠will end right after - maybe before - but it’ll end right ​after the ‌midterms. Gasoline’s going to drop like a rock,” Mr. Trump said.

World.title: Kerala HC grants police protection to journalist Aparna Kurup following cyberattacks over TV Debate involving Kanthapuram’s remarks
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has directed the Kochi City Police Commissioner to ensure protection to life and residence of Aparna Kurup, a journalist in a Malayalam TV Channel.

Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas also instructed the Commissioner to ensure the law and order in the vicinity of Ms. Kurup’s residence without any obstruction or interference until her petition is disposed.

Ms. Kurup had approached the court following alleged cyber attacks and death threats arising from a TV program she had hosted debating the remarks made by Sunni Muslim Scholar Kanthapuram A.P. Aboobacker Musaliyar about women. In her petition, Ms. Kurup claimed that her residence address along with her photograph was published on social media platforms as part of the cyber attacks.

She had approached the Kochi City cyber police and Kochi City Commissioner and filed a complaint on September 7 against the alleged attacks. She claimed that “cadres of certain Islamic fundamentalist organisations including SDPI were actively instigating and sharing her personal details, calling for a protest in front of her house and for physical harm”.

The television debate had led to the registration of a case against Ms. Kurup as well, for making allegedly provocative statements during the TV debate. It was later taken down by the channel. Ms. Kurup was booked by the Kochi City cyber police based on a complaint from B.M. Abdul Hakeem from Kasargod.

World.title: Rajasthan Urban Local Body polls results: BJP edges past Congress; counting under way at many wards
World.content:
The ruling BJP emerged ahead of the Congress in Rajasthan’s urban local body elections on Monday (September 14, 2026), winning 4,179 wards against the opposition party’s 3,613 and securing clear majorities in four of the state’s 10 municipal corporations.

The Congress secured majority in Bikaner Municipal Corporation and scored a major victory in Municipal Council in Jhalawar, considered a stronghold of former chief minister Vasundhara Raje.

Independents emerged as a major force by winning 2,273 wards and dominating the verdict in Municipal Corporation in Bharatpur, the hometown of Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma, where they bagged 36 of the 65 wards.

Bharatpur gave one of the most striking verdicts of the elections as Independents won 36 of the 65 wards, while BJP managed 20 and Congress seven. BSP and RLP won one ward each.

The result assumed political significance as Bharatpur is the hometown of Chief Minister Sharma. As the numbers streamed in, Sharma termed the victory to people’s faith in the BJP, and central leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Mr. Sharma said, “On the auspicious occasion of Ganesh Chaturthi, the people of Rajasthan have delivered a historic verdict, resoundingly endorsing Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat–Viksit Rajasthan’. This magnificent victory reflects the tireless dedication of our karyakartas and the unwavering faith of our citizens. Our youth and women have firmly reaffirmed their trust in the Prime Minister’s leadership. By taking welfare schemes to the grassroots, achieving an 84 per cent public grievance redressal rate, and fulfilling 78% of our manifesto promises, we have honoured public trust. By wholeheartedly embracing ‘One State, One Election’, voters have decisively chosen resource conservation and uninterrupted development. This decisive mandate will pave the way for an even greater victory in the upcoming Panchayat polls.”

Congress on BJP’s winning margins

Congress Rajasthan chief Govind Singh Dotasra, however, claimed that the BJP’s winning margins had thinned against the pattern, even as he blamed an “unfair” delimitation to his party’s narrow losses.

Earlier, even as the vote count was on, Mr. Dotasra accused the BJP of misusing government machinery and police to influence the outcome.

According to figures available on the State Election Commission website, results for 10,235 of the 10,244 wards where counting was being held were declared till 8.30 p.m.

Apart from BJP’s 4,179 and Congress’s 3,613 wards, the Rashtriya Loktantrik Party won 63, AAP 42, CPI(M) 38, BSP 19 and Bharat Adivasi Party eight.

The BJP crossed the majority mark in Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota, and Bhilwara municipal corporations, while the Congress secured a majority in Bikaner.

In Jaipur Municipal Corporation, the BJP won 78 of the 150 wards, Congress won 53, and Independents won 15 wards. Results for four wards were yet to be declared on the SEC website.

The BJP won 53 of the 80 wards in Udaipur, while the Congress secured 23, Independents three and CPI(M) one.

In Bhilwara, the BJP won 45 of the 70 wards against the Congress’s 10, while Independents won 15.

The BJP also crossed the majority mark in Kota, winning 55 wards in the 100-member corporation.

Congress, in Bikaner Municipal Corporation, won 42 of the 80 wards against the BJP’s 27. Independents won 10 and RLP one.

Jodhpur remained on the fence as the BJP and Congress won 44 wards each in the 100-member corporation. Independents won 10 and RLP one, while one result was yet to be declared.

In Ajmer, Congress emerged as the largest party with 37 of the 80 wards against BJP’s 32 and Independents’ 11, leaving no party with a clear majority.

Congress also emerged as the largest party in the municipal corporation of Pali, the hometown of BJP state president Madan Rathore, winning 29 of the 65 wards. The BJP won 21 and Independents 15.

In Alwar, BJP was the largest party with 28 of the 65 wards, followed by Congress with 23, Independents 13 and BSP one.

Congress also scored a notable victory in Jhalawar, a region considered a political stronghold of senior BJP leader Vasundhara Raje.

It won 29 of the 45 wards in Jhalawar Municipal Council, while BJP secured 13, Independents two and AAP one.

The BJP, however, retained its dominance in Jhalrapatan municipality, winning 22 of its 35 wards against Congress’ eight and AAP’s five. Raje, a two-time chief minister, is the sitting BJP MLA from Jhalrapatan.

BJP state president Madan Rathore thanked voters and party workers and described the results as a historic victory for the party. Addressing a press conference here, Dotasra said the BJP has traditionally had an advantage in urban local body polls, particularly when in power, but Monday’s results showed that it failed to retain that edge.

He claimed that the BJP had a vote-share lead of 8.12% points over the Congress during the 2014-16 urban polls under the Vasundhara Raje government, while the Congress had a 2.2% point lead over the BJP during the 2019-21 polls under the Ashok Gehlot government.

“In this election, the BJP’s lead over the Congress is less than one per cent,” he said.

Delimitation of wards

Mr. Dotasra also alleged that the Congress would have won around 1,500 more wards but for irregular and “unfair” delimitation of wards.

The elections were held for 309 urban local bodies comprising 10 municipal corporations, 51 municipal councils and 248 municipalities.

More than 1.44 crore voters were eligible to exercise their franchise in the two-phase polling held on September 9 and 11.

In the previous municipal election cycle held between November 2019 and February 2021, Rajasthan had 196 urban local bodies comprising 7,500 wards.

After the elections for mayors and chairpersons, Congress controlled 123 of the 196 bodies and BJP 64, while Independents and other parties headed nine.

Mayors and chairpersons of the newly elected urban bodies will be elected on September 21, followed by deputy mayors, deputy chairpersons and municipal vice-presidents on September 22.

World.title: Ideological clarity may soon be just a tap away for CPI(M) cadre in Keralam
World.content:
In the coming days, the cadre of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] in Keralam may just need a tap on their mobile phones to clear their ideological confusions.

Developing mobile/web applications to keep party activists updated on political issues is among the suggestions put forward by the participants during the open debate of the party’s ongoing extended State committee meeting in Kozhikode.

According to CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan, the proposal is to strengthen the continuous process of ideological education for the party cadre by including modern technological innovations. Special web and mobile applications need to be designed for the purpose, he said. “Suppose if comrades have doubts related to ideological or political issues, such apps can instantly come to their aid,” Mr. Govindan told the media in Kozhikode on Monday (September 14, 2026) afternoon.

A review report brought out by the party’s Central Committee on the Assembly election debacle in Keralam had highlighted the lack of politicisation within the class and mass organisations. The review report says that both the leadership and the cadre “should be politically very sharp” when they are confronted with an adverse situation and are fighting the reactionary ruling classes, who have ganged up against them.

Quoting the review report on the elections prepared by the State committee, the Central Committee had noted “the decline in the number of comrades capable of presenting our political perspectives to the people” and “the lack of adequate politicisation taking place within class and mass organisations”, terming it as a “major organisational weakness.” The report says that even though many classes were conducted against communalism, the party had been unable to convert it into a public consciousness.

The three-day extended State committee meeting, which began on Sunday (September 13, 2026), is being held to address the organisational and political weaknesses of the CPI(M) against the backdrop of the dismal performance of the party-led Left Democratic Front in the Assembly polls in Keralam. Apart from State committee members, district secretariat members from across the State and leaders of the party’s class and mass organisations are attending it.

Mr. Govindan had earlier on Sunday (September 13, 2026) presented a draft document prepared by the State committee on the corrective steps required to energise the organisation. Following that, the participants engaged in district-level group discussions. Later, an hour-long open debate by select delegates too was held in the night. The open debate continued on Monday (September 14, 2026) as well.

Criticisms in open debate

Talking to the media on Monday (September 14, 2026), Mr. Govindan admitted that fierce criticisms were levelled against the party leadership during the debate, though he did not divulge the details. According to sources, the delegates from across districts sought stronger corrective steps to address the organisational weaknesses. There were also demands to fix accountability on the leadership for the Assembly election debacle.

Mr. Govindan, meanwhile, said that another suggestion had been given to form a collective of like-minded organisations, including human rights groups, to resist the unfair targeting of party leaders by Central agencies.

This could be significant because just around a week before the CPI(M) meeting began in Kozhikode, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) had sent a letter to the Keralam State Police Chief seeking registration of a first information report against Opposition leader and CPI(M) Polit Bureau member Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T. Veena, and her husband and Beypore MLA P.A. Mohamed Riyas in the CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case. Without mentioning the ED’s move, party general secretary M.A. Baby had made a passing reference to the activities of the Central agencies during his inaugural speech on Sunday (September 13, 2026). On the same day, however, Mr. Govindan explicitly referred to the agency’s action as an attack against the party.

The extended meeting is slated to conclude on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) afternoon, with Mr. Govindan responding to the remarks made during the open debate. He will also present a report after adding the suggestions proposed by the delegates for the rectification process in the draft document mentioned earlier. This will be followed by a mass rally at the Kozhikode beach in the evening.

World.title: Maharashtra govt. orders probe into land transfer to Premier Automobiles over six decades ago
World.content:
An investigation has been ordered into the allotment of about 175 acres land by Maharashtra government to Premier Automobile Ltd (Now renamed Premier Ltd) more than six decades ago and the subsequent transfer of land parcels by the company to real estate developers and other entities.

Premier Automobiles was synonymous with the iconic Fiat 1100 D, the Premier Padmini car as well as Premier 118NE.

Following allegations of cattle-grazing land allotted for industrial purpose in 1960s turning into premium real estate in alleged land use violation, the Maharashtra Revenue Department has constituted a nine-member Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by the Konkan Divisional Commissioner, to examine the alleged transfer of government-owned grazing land in Kalyan taluka, Thane district near Mumbai.

The government order, issued on September 4, follows directions given at a meeting chaired by Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule on August 19, 2026.

The Minister was hearing complaints concerning parcels of cattle-grazing land in Mangaon, Kole, Katai, Gharivali, Sandap and Usarghar villages. The complaints trace the original transactions to 1960s the period when Maharashtra was seeking to promote industrialisation and attract manufacturing activity.

Premier Automobiles, one of the pioneers in automobile assembling belonging to the Walchand Group, was then expanding from it’s original factory in Kurla in Suburban Mumbai to this location in Kalyan-Dombivali.

SIT to scrutinise government and grazing-land records

The SIT has been asked to scrutinise original government and grazing-land records and examine transfers made through gram panchayats to Premier Automobiles and then to other entities.

These include Lodha Developers, Anant Developers and Jupiter Life Line Hospital. A separate term dealing with third-party sales names Out N Out Infotech and Sundarniwas Properties.

These land parcels were previously owned by Premier Automobiles and later monetised to repay debt and to invest in it’s plant in Pune.

Inquiry to cover five broad issues

The inquiry will cover five broad issues: the original status of the land and manner of transfer; conversion of parcels from Occupant Class II to Occupant Class I; the validity of entries in the record of rights, including 7/12 extracts and mutation entries; subsequent sale transactions; and action to be recommended if responsibility is established.

The SIT has also been asked to examine whether the conversion of tenure and the calculation or adjustment of the unearned amount payable to the government complied with applicable orders and rules.

It must determine whether any government land was encroached upon or whether official powers were misused.
